spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m3p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cranes, Apron, MaxEpoch

NoLeader == "vacant"

VARIABLES leader, epoch, permit, onApron, waiting

vars == <<leader, epoch, permit, onApron, waiting>>

\* permit[c] is the epoch in which crane c was authorised to place one box;
\* 0 means no authorisation at all, and a permit from an older epoch is void.
Live == {c \in Cranes : permit[c] = epoch}

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Cranes \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
  /\ permit \in [Cranes -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ onApron \in 0..Apron
  /\ waiting \in [Cranes -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ permit = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
  /\ onApron = 0
  /\ waiting = [c \in Cranes |-> FALSE]

RequestSlot(c) ==
  /\ ~waiting[c]
  /\ permit[c] = 0
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, permit, onApron>>

\* The leader reserves apron space up front, so a permit counts against capacity
\* from the moment it is issued until the box actually lands.
Authorise(c) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ waiting[c]
  /\ permit[c] # epoch
  /\ onApron + Cardinality(Live) < Apron
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, onApron, waiting>>

Refuse(c) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ waiting[c]
  /\ permit[c] # epoch
  /\ onApron + Cardinality(Live) >= Apron
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, onApron>>

Land(c) ==
  /\ waiting[c]
  /\ permit[c] = epoch
  /\ onApron' = onApron + 1
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch>>

\* A permit stamped by a superseded leader carries no reservation and is dropped.
Expire(c) ==
  /\ permit[c] # 0
  /\ permit[c] # epoch
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![c] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, onApron, waiting>>

Depart ==
  /\ onApron > 0
  /\ onApron' = onApron - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, permit, waiting>>

Elect(c) ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ leader' = c
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<permit, onApron, waiting>>

\* Failure is only modelled while a replacement election is still affordable,
\* so the yard is never left permanently without a controller.
LeaderFail ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch - 1
  /\ leader' = NoLeader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, permit, onApron, waiting>>

AdminInstall(c) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ leader # c
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ leader' = c
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<permit, onApron, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cranes :
       RequestSlot(c) \/ Authorise(c) \/ Refuse(c) \/ Land(c)
         \/ Expire(c) \/ Elect(c) \/ AdminInstall(c)
  \/ Depart
  \/ LeaderFail

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Cranes : Elect(c))
  /\ \A c \in Cranes : SF_vars(Authorise(c) \/ Refuse(c) \/ Land(c))

CapacityHonoured ==
  onApron + Cardinality(Live) <= Apron

RequestsSettle ==
  \A c \in Cranes : waiting[c] ~> ~waiting[c]

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {c1, c2}
    Apron = 2
    MaxEpoch = 4
INVARIANT CapacityHonoured
PROPERTY RequestsSettle
nl:
A container-ship crane yard keeps a landing apron between the quay cranes and the
stacking blocks, and that apron physically holds only a fixed number of boxes at once.
Every crane that wants to set a box down on the apron must first be authorised by the
yard's current shift controller, and the controllers run a leader-election protocol among
themselves: exactly one controller is the acting leader, the leadership is stamped with a
monotone epoch number, and if the acting leader drops off the radio net the remaining
controllers elect a replacement under a fresh epoch. Yard management also keeps a
privileged override: a dispatcher at the terminal operations centre may push a chosen
controller into the leader seat directly, without waiting for the incumbent to fail, and
that override also advances the epoch.

Because authorisations are epoch-stamped, an authorisation issued by a controller that has
since been replaced is void, and the crane holding it must throw it away rather than act
on it. The acting leader hands out an authorisation only when the boxes already sitting on
the apron plus the authorisations that are still live under the current epoch leave room
for one more; when there is no room, the leader turns the request down and the crane must
ask again later. Boxes are eventually hauled off the apron into the stacks, which frees
space back up.

The full action set is: RequestSlot (a crane asks for apron space), Authorise (the acting
leader stamps that crane with an authorisation carrying the current epoch, but only while
occupied space plus live authorisations leaves headroom), Refuse (the acting leader turns
a waiting crane away because the apron is committed to capacity), Land (a crane with a
current-epoch authorisation actually sets its box on the apron), Expire (a crane discards
an authorisation whose epoch has been superseded), Depart (a box is hauled off the apron
into the stacks), Elect (a controller takes the vacant leader seat under a new epoch),
LeaderFail (the acting leader drops off the net, vacating the seat), and AdminInstall (the
terminal operations dispatcher overrides the election and installs a chosen controller
under a new epoch).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of boxes on the apron plus the number of authorisations that are still live under the current epoch never exceeds the apron's fixed capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every crane that asks for apron space eventually has its request settled, either by landing its box or by being turned away.

---- MODULE W4Od7m2p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Planners, Participants, Pool, Batch

VARIABLES phase, ballot, setAside, energised

vars == <<phase, ballot, setAside, energised>>

RECURSIVE SumOf(_, _)
SumOf(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOf(f, S \ {x})

\* Sockets held by an in-flight round count against the shared pool exactly like
\* sockets that are already energised -- that is what makes the two instances safe.
Committed == SumOf(energised, Planners)
Provisional == SumOf(setAside, Planners)

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in [Planners -> {"idle", "voting"}]
  /\ ballot \in [Planners -> [Participants -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]]
  /\ setAside \in [Planners -> 0..Pool]
  /\ energised \in [Planners -> 0..Pool]

Init ==
  /\ phase = [p \in Planners |-> "idle"]
  /\ ballot = [p \in Planners |-> [q \in Participants |-> "none"]]
  /\ setAside = [p \in Planners |-> 0]
  /\ energised = [p \in Planners |-> 0]

\* The coordinator sizes the batch against the whole pool, not just its own books.
BeginRound(p) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "idle"
  /\ Committed + Provisional + Batch <= Pool
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "voting"]
  /\ setAside' = [setAside EXCEPT ![p] = Batch]
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![p] = [q \in Participants |-> "none"]]
  /\ UNCHANGED energised

VoteYes(p, q) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "voting"
  /\ ballot[p][q] = "none"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![p][q] = "yes"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, setAside, energised>>

VoteNo(p, q) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "voting"
  /\ ballot[p][q] = "none"
  /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![p][q] = "no"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, setAside, energised>>

CommitRound(p) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "voting"
  /\ \A q \in Participants : ballot[p][q] = "yes"
  /\ energised' = [energised EXCEPT ![p] = energised[p] + setAside[p]]
  /\ setAside' = [setAside EXCEPT ![p] = 0]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED ballot

AbortRound(p) ==
  /\ phase[p] = "voting"
  /\ \E q \in Participants : ballot[p][q] = "no"
  /\ setAside' = [setAside EXCEPT ![p] = 0]
  /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![p] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, energised>>

FreeSocket(p) ==
  /\ energised[p] > 0
  /\ energised' = [energised EXCEPT ![p] = energised[p] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, setAside>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Planners : BeginRound(p) \/ CommitRound(p) \/ AbortRound(p) \/ FreeSocket(p)
  \/ \E p \in Planners, q \in Participants : VoteYes(p, q) \/ VoteNo(p, q)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Neither instance may push the shared pool past its physical socket count.
PoolNotOversubscribed ==
  Committed + Provisional <= Pool

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Planners = {import, export}
    Participants = {quay, stack, tech}
    Pool = 4
    Batch = 2
INVARIANT PoolNotOversubscribed
nl:
The reefer plugs at a container-ship crane yard are a single shared pool: a fixed number
of powered sockets on the quay, and no more. Two independent yard-planning instances --
one driving the import stacks, one driving the export stacks -- both draw from that same
socket pool, and neither is aware of the other's bookings except through the pool total.
Each instance books sockets for a batch of reefer boxes using a two-phase commit across
its own participants: the yard planner acts as coordinator, opens a round by provisionally
setting aside a batch of sockets, and then collects a vote from each participant (the quay
crane, the stack crane, the reefer technician). Only if every participant votes yes does
the round commit and the set-aside sockets become genuinely energised; a single no vote
aborts the round and hands the set-aside sockets straight back.

The crucial accounting rule is that sockets which are merely set aside for a round that is
still voting are just as unavailable as sockets already energised, and this holds across
both instances at once. A coordinator may therefore only open a new round when the sockets
already energised, plus every socket set aside by either instance's in-flight round, still
leave room for the whole batch. Energised sockets are freed one at a time as reefer boxes
are collected by their consignees.

The full action set is: BeginRound (an instance's coordinator opens a two-phase round and
provisionally sets aside a batch of sockets, only if the shared pool has room for the
batch on top of everything already energised or set aside), VoteYes (a participant of an
in-flight round votes to commit), VoteNo (a participant of an in-flight round votes to
abort), CommitRound (a round whose participants have all voted yes turns its set-aside
sockets into energised sockets), AbortRound (a round with at least one no vote returns its
set-aside sockets to the pool untouched), and FreeSocket (an energised socket is released
when its reefer box is collected).
SAFETY PROPERTY: across both yard-planning instances together, the sockets already energised plus the sockets provisionally set aside by in-flight two-phase rounds never exceed the size of the shared socket pool.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m1p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumCars, Rating, MaxDraw, MaxOverride

Cars == 1..NumCars
Nxt(i) == IF i = NumCars THEN 1 ELSE i + 1

VARIABLES token, wants, running, draw, overrides

vars == <<token, wants, running, draw, overrides>>

\* Feeder load is the sum of the amp-units drawn by the cars that are actually running.
RECURSIVE Drawn(_)
Drawn(k) == IF k = 0 THEN 0
            ELSE (IF running[k] THEN draw[k] ELSE 0) + Drawn(k - 1)

Used == Drawn(NumCars)

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Cars
  /\ wants \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ running \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ draw \in [Cars -> 0..MaxDraw]
  /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverride

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ wants = [i \in Cars |-> FALSE]
  /\ running = [i \in Cars |-> FALSE]
  /\ draw = [i \in Cars |-> 0]
  /\ overrides = 0

RequestRun(i) ==
  /\ ~wants[i]
  /\ ~running[i]
  /\ \E d \in 1..MaxDraw : draw' = [draw EXCEPT ![i] = d]
  /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, running, overrides>>

\* Only the token holder commits to a run, and only into real feeder headroom.
StartRun(i) ==
  /\ token = i
  /\ wants[i]
  /\ Used + draw[i] <= Rating
  /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
  /\ wants' = [wants EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, draw, overrides>>

FinishRun(i) ==
  /\ running[i]
  /\ running' = [running EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
  /\ draw' = [draw EXCEPT ![i] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, wants, overrides>>

\* The holder keeps the token while it still has an unstarted request, so a car
\* short of headroom waits at the head of the ring instead of losing its turn.
PassToken ==
  /\ ~wants[token]
  /\ token' = Nxt(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wants, running, draw, overrides>>

AdminHandToken(j) ==
  /\ overrides < MaxOverride
  /\ j # token
  /\ token' = j
  /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wants, running, draw>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Cars : RequestRun(i) \/ StartRun(i) \/ FinishRun(i) \/ AdminHandToken(i)
  \/ PassToken

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(PassToken)
  /\ \A i \in Cars : SF_vars(StartRun(i))
  /\ \A i \in Cars : WF_vars(FinishRun(i))

FeederWithinRating == Used <= Rating

\* The ring plus the wait-with-the-token rule means no car is passed over forever.
EveryRequestStarts ==
  \A i \in Cars : wants[i] ~> running[i]

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumCars = 3
    Rating = 3
    MaxDraw = 2
    MaxOverride = 2
INVARIANT FeederWithinRating
PROPERTY EveryRequestStarts
nl:
The elevator bank in a skyscraper shares one hoist power feeder, and that feeder can
sustain only a limited number of amp-units of acceleration at any instant. Each car, when
it takes on a run, draws a known number of amp-units for the whole duration of that run,
and heavy cars draw more than light ones. To keep the total draw inside the feeder's
rating, the bank uses a dispatch token that circulates around the cars in a fixed ring:
car 1 hands it to car 2, car 2 to car 3, and the last car hands it back to car 1. Only the
car currently holding the token is allowed to commit itself to a run, and it may do so
only if its own draw fits in whatever headroom the feeder has left after the cars already
running. A car that wants a run but finds no headroom simply keeps the token and waits for
running cars to finish, which is why the token is not passed on while its holder still has
an unstarted run pending.

The building engineer holds a privileged override: with the fire-service key, the token
can be pulled out of the ring and handed straight to a nominated car, skipping the normal
rotation. The override is deliberately restricted to a small number of uses per
service period so that the ordinary rotation is not defeated.

The full action set is: RequestRun (a car registers that it wants a run and fixes the
amp-units it will draw), StartRun (the token holder with a pending request commits to its
run, provided its draw fits in the feeder's remaining headroom), FinishRun (a running car
completes and gives its amp-units back to the feeder), PassToken (a token holder with no
pending request hands the token to the next car in the ring), and AdminHandToken (the
building engineer uses the fire-service key to move the token directly to a nominated car,
consuming one of the limited overrides).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total amp-units drawn by all cars currently running never exceeds the hoist feeder's rating.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every car that registers a request for a run eventually gets that run started.

---- MODULE W4Od2m8p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Robots, NumAisles, NumBays

Aisles == 1..NumAisles
Slots == Aisles \X (1..NumBays)
NoSlot == <<0, 0>>
Free == "free"

VARIABLES aisleOwner, holdSlot, mesh, task

vars == <<aisleOwner, holdSlot, mesh, task>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ aisleOwner \in [Aisles -> Robots \cup {Free}]
  /\ holdSlot \in [Robots -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
  /\ mesh \subseteq (Robots \X Slots)
  /\ task \in [Robots -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]

Init ==
  /\ aisleOwner = [a \in Aisles |-> Free]
  /\ holdSlot = [r \in Robots |-> NoSlot]
  /\ mesh = {}
  /\ task = [r \in Robots |-> NoSlot]

Idle(r) ==
  /\ task[r] = NoSlot
  /\ holdSlot[r] = NoSlot
  /\ ~\E m \in mesh : m[1] = r

PickTask(r, s) ==
  /\ Idle(r)
  /\ task' = [task EXCEPT ![r] = s]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleOwner, holdSlot, mesh>>

\* Coarse level: the whole aisle must be taken before any bay inside it.
TakeAisle(r) ==
  /\ task[r] # NoSlot
  /\ aisleOwner[task[r][1]] = Free
  /\ aisleOwner' = [aisleOwner EXCEPT ![task[r][1]] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holdSlot, mesh, task>>

\* The mesh is an unordered bag: a posted allocation may arrive at any later moment.
PostRequest(r) ==
  /\ task[r] # NoSlot
  /\ aisleOwner[task[r][1]] = r
  /\ mesh' = mesh \cup {<<r, task[r]>>}
  /\ task' = [task EXCEPT ![r] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleOwner, holdSlot>>

\* Delivery re-checks the coarse lock, because the message may be out of date.
DeliverGrant(r, s) ==
  /\ <<r, s>> \in mesh
  /\ aisleOwner[s[1]] = r
  /\ \A q \in Robots : holdSlot[q] # s
  /\ holdSlot' = [holdSlot EXCEPT ![r] = s]
  /\ mesh' = mesh \ {<<r, s>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleOwner, task>>

DropStale(r, s) ==
  /\ <<r, s>> \in mesh
  /\ (aisleOwner[s[1]] # r \/ \E q \in Robots : holdSlot[q] = s)
  /\ mesh' = mesh \ {<<r, s>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleOwner, holdSlot, task>>

ReleaseSlot(r) ==
  /\ holdSlot[r] # NoSlot
  /\ holdSlot' = [holdSlot EXCEPT ![r] = NoSlot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<aisleOwner, mesh, task>>

\* An aisle cannot change hands while its owner still holds a bay inside it.
ReleaseAisle(r, a) ==
  /\ aisleOwner[a] = r
  /\ ~(holdSlot[r] # NoSlot /\ holdSlot[r][1] = a)
  /\ aisleOwner' = [aisleOwner EXCEPT ![a] = Free]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holdSlot, mesh, task>>

Next ==
  \/ \E r \in Robots, s \in Slots : PickTask(r, s) \/ DeliverGrant(r, s) \/ DropStale(r, s)
  \/ \E r \in Robots : TakeAisle(r) \/ PostRequest(r) \/ ReleaseSlot(r)
  \/ \E r \in Robots, a \in Aisles : ReleaseAisle(r, a)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

AllocationBackedByAisle ==
  \A r \in Robots : holdSlot[r] # NoSlot => aisleOwner[holdSlot[r][1]] = r

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2}
    NumAisles = 2
    NumBays = 2
INVARIANT AllocationBackedByAisle
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet picks from bin slots that are grouped into aisles. To stop two
robots from ever being handed the same bin slot, the fleet controller uses a two-level
locking discipline: a robot must first take the coarse lock on a whole aisle, and only
then may it be allocated individual fine-grained slots inside that aisle. An aisle lock is
exclusive, so if the discipline is respected the slots inside an aisle can only ever be
allocated to the robot that currently owns the aisle.

The complication is the radio link. When a robot asks for a slot, the controller's
allocation message goes into the fleet's mesh network, and the mesh delivers messages in
whatever order it likes -- an allocation posted early can arrive after an aisle lock has
already been given up and re-taken by somebody else. The discipline therefore re-checks
the coarse lock at the moment of delivery rather than trusting the message: an allocation
that arrives when the addressee no longer owns the relevant aisle is thrown away instead
of being honoured. A robot is also forbidden from releasing an aisle lock while it still
holds slots inside that aisle, so an aisle can never change hands underneath an
outstanding allocation.

The full action set is: PickTask (an idle robot chooses a bin slot it wants to work on),
TakeAisle (a robot with a chosen slot takes the free coarse lock on that slot's aisle),
PostRequest (a robot that owns the aisle puts an allocation request for its chosen slot
onto the mesh, where it will be delivered in an arbitrary order), DeliverGrant (a mesh
message arrives and, because the addressee still owns the aisle and the slot is
unallocated, the slot is allocated to it), DropStale (a mesh message arrives to a robot
that no longer owns the aisle and is discarded), ReleaseSlot (a robot gives up one of its
allocated slots), and ReleaseAisle (a robot with no remaining slots in an aisle gives up
the coarse lock).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every bin slot allocated to a robot lies in an aisle whose coarse lock is currently held by that same robot, so no slot can be allocated to two robots at once.

---- MODULE W4Od16m9p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Stations, Writes, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, stage, stamp, confirmed, seen

vars == <<epoch, stage, stamp, confirmed, seen>>

InRecord == {w \in Writes : stage[w] = "applied"}

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
  /\ stage \in [Writes -> {"idle", "staged", "applied", "void"}]
  /\ stamp \in [Writes -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ confirmed \in [Stations -> SUBSET Writes]
  /\ seen \in [Stations -> 1..MaxEpoch]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ stage = [w \in Writes |-> "idle"]
  /\ stamp = [w \in Writes |-> 0]
  /\ confirmed = [s \in Stations |-> {}]
  /\ seen = [s \in Stations |-> 1]

StageWrite(w) ==
  /\ stage[w] = "idle"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = "staged"]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![w] = epoch]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, confirmed, seen>>

ApplyWrite(w) ==
  /\ stage[w] = "staged"
  /\ stamp[w] = epoch
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = "applied"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stamp, confirmed, seen>>

\* A write staged under a superseded arrangement is dropped, never applied.
VoidWrite(w) ==
  /\ stage[w] = "staged"
  /\ stamp[w] # epoch
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = "void"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stamp, confirmed, seen>>

\* A station that has fallen behind must catch up before it may confirm anything.
ConfirmWrite(s, w) ==
  /\ stage[w] = "applied"
  /\ seen[s] = epoch
  /\ w \notin confirmed[s]
  /\ confirmed' = [confirmed EXCEPT ![s] = confirmed[s] \cup {w}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stage, stamp, seen>>

\* Reconfiguration may unwind a stale application, but a confirmed write is pinned.
RollBack(w) ==
  /\ stage[w] = "applied"
  /\ stamp[w] # epoch
  /\ \A s \in Stations : w \notin confirmed[s]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = "void"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stamp, confirmed, seen>>

\* Handing the medicine over closes the record entry and the confirmations with it.
Collect(w) ==
  /\ stage[w] = "applied"
  /\ \E s \in Stations : w \in confirmed[s]
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
  /\ confirmed' = [s \in Stations |-> confirmed[s] \ {w}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, seen>>

Recycle(w) ==
  /\ stage[w] = "void"
  /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
  /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, confirmed, seen>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<stage, stamp, confirmed, seen>>

CatchUp(s) ==
  /\ seen[s] < epoch
  /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![s] = seen[s] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, stage, stamp, confirmed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E w \in Writes : StageWrite(w) \/ ApplyWrite(w) \/ VoidWrite(w) \/ RollBack(w)
                         \/ Collect(w) \/ Recycle(w)
  \/ \E s \in Stations, w \in Writes : ConfirmWrite(s, w)
  \/ \E s \in Stations : CatchUp(s)
  \/ Reconfigure

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A w \in Writes : WF_vars(ApplyWrite(w) \/ VoidWrite(w))

\* No confirmed write is ever lost from the shared record.
ConfirmedWritesSurvive ==
  \A s \in Stations : confirmed[s] \subseteq InRecord

StagedWritesSettle ==
  \A w \in Writes : (stage[w] = "staged") ~> (stage[w] \in {"applied", "void"})

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Stations = {counter, window}
    Writes = {w1, w2}
    MaxEpoch = 3
INVARIANT ConfirmedWritesSurvive
PROPERTY StagedWritesSettle
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser keeps one shared medication record per patient, and
several dispensing stations write to it: the main counter, the drive-through window, and
the ward trolley. The stations do not vote among themselves; instead the pharmacy runs an
epoch-numbered reconfiguration. Every write is stamped with the epoch that was current
when it was staged, and whenever the pharmacist-in-charge rearranges the workflow -- a
station is moved to a different terminal, the label printer is swapped -- the epoch is
bumped, which retroactively invalidates any write still in flight from the old
arrangement. A write staged under a superseded epoch is voided rather than applied,
because the arrangement it assumed no longer exists.

None of the stations ever fails. What they do is fall behind: a station can be slow,
running one or more epochs behind the pharmacist's current arrangement, and it catches up
one epoch at a time. A slow station is not allowed to confirm anything to the patient
until it has caught up to the current epoch, so its confirmations always reflect the
arrangement that is actually in force.

The rule that protects the record is about confirmations. Once a station has confirmed a
write to the patient -- printed the label, handed over the bag -- that write must stay in
the record. Reconfiguration is therefore allowed to roll back a write that was applied
under a stale epoch, but only while no station has yet confirmed it; a confirmed write is
pinned and survives every later reconfiguration.

The full action set is: StageWrite (a station stages a change to the shared record,
stamping it with the current epoch), ApplyWrite (a staged write whose stamp is still
current is applied to the record), VoidWrite (a staged write whose stamp has been
superseded is discarded unapplied), ConfirmWrite (a station that has caught up to the
current epoch confirms an applied write to the patient), RollBack (reconfiguration
discards an applied write whose stamp is stale, permitted only when no station has
confirmed it), Collect (the patient takes the medicine, which closes that entry in the
record and clears the confirmations that went with it), Recycle (a voided write is handed
back to its station to be staged again), Reconfigure (the pharmacist-in-charge bumps the
epoch), and CatchUp (a slow station advances its view by one epoch).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every write that some station has confirmed to the patient is still present in the shared medication record.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every staged write is eventually settled, either applied to the record or voided as stale.

CONSTANTS Crews, Cabinets, NumColumns

Columns == 1..NumColumns
Jobs == Cabinets \X Columns
NoJob == "none"
Unlocked == "unlocked"

VARIABLES cabLock, claimed, inService, chosen

vars == <<cabLock, claimed, inService, chosen>>

\* The columns a crew is entitled to hold: in service, inside a cabinet it owns.
Grantable(k) ==
  {j \in Jobs : cabLock[j[1]] = k /\ j[2] \in inService[j[1]]}

TypeOK ==
  /\ cabLock \in [Cabinets -> Crews \cup {Unlocked}]
  /\ claimed \in [Crews -> SUBSET Jobs]
  /\ inService \in [Cabinets -> SUBSET Columns]
  /\ chosen \in [Crews -> Jobs \cup {NoJob}]

Init ==
  /\ cabLock = [b \in Cabinets |-> Unlocked]
  /\ claimed = [k \in Crews |-> {}]
  /\ inService = [b \in Cabinets |-> Columns]
  /\ chosen = [k \in Crews |-> NoJob]

PickJob(k, j) ==
  /\ chosen[k] = NoJob
  /\ chosen' = [chosen EXCEPT ![k] = j]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabLock, claimed, inService>>

\* Coarse first: the cabinet lock is exclusive and must precede any column work.
TakeCabinet(k) ==
  /\ chosen[k] # NoJob
  /\ cabLock[chosen[k][1]] = Unlocked
  /\ cabLock' = [cabLock EXCEPT ![chosen[k][1]] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, inService, chosen>>

ClaimColumn(k) ==
  /\ chosen[k] # NoJob
  /\ cabLock[chosen[k][1]] = k
  /\ chosen[k][2] \in inService[chosen[k][1]]
  /\ \A q \in Crews : chosen[k] \notin claimed[q]
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![k] = claimed[k] \cup {chosen[k]}]
  /\ chosen' = [chosen EXCEPT ![k] = NoJob]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabLock, inService>>

FinishColumn(k, j) ==
  /\ j \in claimed[k]
  /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![k] = claimed[k] \ {j}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabLock, inService, chosen>>

\* A cabinet cannot change hands while its owner still holds column assignments.
ReleaseCabinet(k, b) ==
  /\ cabLock[b] = k
  /\ \A j \in claimed[k] : j[1] # b
  /\ cabLock' = [cabLock EXCEPT ![b] = Unlocked]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<claimed, inService, chosen>>

\* Capacity shrinks at runtime, but never underneath a live assignment.
WithdrawColumn(b, c) ==
  /\ c \in inService[b]
  /\ \A q \in Crews : <<b, c>> \notin claimed[q]
  /\ inService' = [inService EXCEPT ![b] = inService[b] \ {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabLock, claimed, chosen>>

RestoreColumn(b, c) ==
  /\ c \notin inService[b]
  /\ inService' = [inService EXCEPT ![b] = inService[b] \cup {c}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabLock, claimed, chosen>>

Next ==
  \/ \E k \in Crews, j \in Jobs : PickJob(k, j) \/ FinishColumn(k, j)
  \/ \E k \in Crews : TakeCabinet(k) \/ ClaimColumn(k)
  \/ \E k \in Crews, b \in Cabinets : ReleaseCabinet(k, b)
  \/ \E b \in Cabinets, c \in Columns : WithdrawColumn(b, c) \/ RestoreColumn(b, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ClaimsWithinOwnedCabinets ==
  \A k \in Crews : claimed[k] \subseteq Grantable(k)

nl:
A vending machine network is serviced by restock crews. Each machine is a cabinet holding
several product columns, and a column is the unit of work: a crew is assigned individual
columns to refill. To stop two crews from being handed the same column, the network's
dispatcher uses a two-level locking discipline. The coarse level is the whole cabinet: a
crew must first take the cabinet lock, which is exclusive. The fine level is the
individual column: only once a crew owns the cabinet may it be assigned columns inside it,
and only columns that are actually in service.

Column capacity is not fixed. Columns are pulled out of service at runtime -- a jammed
spiral, a product line discontinued, a chiller compartment shut down -- and brought back
into service later, so the set of usable columns in a cabinet changes while crews are
working. The discipline is that a column may only be withdrawn from service when no crew
currently holds an assignment for it, because a withdrawn column must never leave a live
assignment stranded. Likewise a crew may not give up a cabinet lock while it still holds
an assignment on any column of that cabinet, so a cabinet cannot change hands underneath
outstanding fine-grained work.

The full action set is: PickJob (an idle crew chooses a column it intends to refill),
TakeCabinet (a crew with a chosen column takes the free coarse lock on that column's
cabinet), ClaimColumn (a crew that owns the cabinet is assigned its chosen column, which
must be in service and unassigned), FinishColumn (a crew completes a refill and gives up
that column assignment), ReleaseCabinet (a crew with no remaining assignments in a cabinet
gives up the coarse lock), WithdrawColumn (the dispatcher takes an unassigned column out
of service, shrinking the cabinet's usable capacity), and RestoreColumn (the dispatcher
puts a column back into service).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every column assignment a crew holds is for a column that is in service in a cabinet whose coarse lock that same crew currently owns, so no column can be assigned to two crews at once.

---- MODULE W4Od13m9p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Machines, Reserve, MaxTopUp, MaxEpoch

VARIABLES epoch, mstate, grantAmt, grantEpoch, held, dark

vars == <<epoch, mstate, grantAmt, grantEpoch, held, dark>>

RECURSIVE SumOf(_, _)
SumOf(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOf(f, S \ {x})

\* Only authorisations stamped with the live epoch still lay claim to the reserve;
\* an older stamp has been invalidated by reconfiguration and can never be collected.
OnStreet == SumOf(held, Machines)
Outstanding ==
  SumOf([m \in Machines |-> IF grantEpoch[m] = epoch THEN grantAmt[m] ELSE 0], Machines)

TypeOK ==
  /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
  /\ mstate \in [Machines -> {"idle", "asking", "granted"}]
  /\ grantAmt \in [Machines -> 0..MaxTopUp]
  /\ grantEpoch \in [Machines -> 0..MaxEpoch]
  /\ held \in [Machines -> 0..Reserve]
  /\ dark \in [Machines -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ mstate = [m \in Machines |-> "idle"]
  /\ grantAmt = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ grantEpoch = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ held = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
  /\ dark = [m \in Machines |-> FALSE]

RequestTopUp(m) ==
  /\ ~dark[m]
  /\ mstate[m] = "idle"
  /\ mstate' = [mstate EXCEPT ![m] = "asking"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, grantAmt, grantEpoch, held, dark>>

\* The depot sizes a grant against floats already out plus every live authorisation.
Authorise(m, a) ==
  /\ mstate[m] = "asking"
  /\ OnStreet + Outstanding + a <= Reserve
  /\ grantAmt' = [grantAmt EXCEPT ![m] = a]
  /\ grantEpoch' = [grantEpoch EXCEPT ![m] = epoch]
  /\ mstate' = [mstate EXCEPT ![m] = "granted"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, held, dark>>

Collect(m) ==
  /\ ~dark[m]
  /\ mstate[m] = "granted"
  /\ grantEpoch[m] = epoch
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m] = held[m] + grantAmt[m]]
  /\ grantAmt' = [grantAmt EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ grantEpoch' = [grantEpoch EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ mstate' = [mstate EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, dark>>

\* The depot cannot tell a dark machine from a slow one, so any grant may be written off.
Timeout(m) ==
  /\ mstate[m] = "granted"
  /\ grantAmt' = [grantAmt EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ grantEpoch' = [grantEpoch EXCEPT ![m] = 0]
  /\ mstate' = [mstate EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, held, dark>>

SpendFloat(m) ==
  /\ held[m] > 0
  /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![m] = held[m] - 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, mstate, grantAmt, grantEpoch, dark>>

Reconfigure ==
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<mstate, grantAmt, grantEpoch, held, dark>>

GoDark(m) ==
  /\ \A q \in Machines : ~dark[q]
  /\ dark' = [dark EXCEPT ![m] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, mstate, grantAmt, grantEpoch, held>>

Next ==
  \/ \E m \in Machines :
       RequestTopUp(m) \/ Collect(m) \/ Timeout(m) \/ SpendFloat(m) \/ GoDark(m)
  \/ \E m \in Machines, a \in 1..MaxTopUp : Authorise(m, a)
  \/ Reconfigure

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A m \in Machines : WF_vars(Collect(m) \/ Timeout(m))

ReserveNotOverdrawn == OnStreet + Outstanding <= Reserve

GrantsSettle ==
  \A m \in Machines : (mstate[m] = "granted") ~> (mstate[m] # "granted")

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2}
    Reserve = 3
    MaxTopUp = 2
    MaxEpoch = 3
INVARIANT ReserveNotOverdrawn
PROPERTY GrantsSettle
nl:
The machines in a vending machine network each keep a coin float so they can give change,
and those floats are drawn from one regional cash reserve of fixed size. The depot cannot
put more cash on the street than the reserve holds, counting both the floats already
sitting inside machines and the top-ups it has authorised but not yet handed over to a
driver. Authorisation is governed by an epoch-numbered reconfiguration: the depot's route
plan carries an epoch number, and every top-up authorisation is stamped with the epoch
current when it was granted. When the route plan is reconfigured the epoch advances, and
any authorisation still stamped with an older epoch stops counting against the reserve and
can no longer be collected.

One machine in the network can go dark without warning: its modem dies, it stops reporting,
and it will never collect the top-up it was promised. The depot cannot tell a silent
machine from a merely slow one, so it does not try. Instead it may time out any
outstanding authorisation, stale or not, writing it off and taking that money straight
back into the reserve. A machine that has gone dark still dispenses product and still pays
out change from the float it already holds; what it can no longer do is talk to the depot,
so it never collects anything more.

The full action set is: RequestTopUp (a machine that is short of change asks the depot for
a float top-up of some amount), Authorise (the depot grants a machine a top-up stamped
with the current epoch, but only if the floats already held plus every authorisation still
valid under the current epoch leave that much of the reserve free), Collect (a machine
that has not gone dark takes up an authorisation still stamped with the current epoch and
adds it to its float), Timeout (the depot writes off an outstanding authorisation and
returns that money to the reserve), SpendFloat (a machine, dark or not, pays out change
and its float falls by one), Reconfigure (the depot revises the route plan and advances
the epoch, invalidating every authorisation stamped with an older epoch), and GoDark (the
one machine that can fail silently loses its modem).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the coin floats held by all machines plus every top-up authorisation still stamped with the current epoch never exceed the regional cash reserve.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every outstanding top-up authorisation is eventually settled, either collected by its machine or timed out by the depot.

---- MODULE W4Od4m1p6t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumCtrls, Bays, MaxRound

Ctrls == 1..NumCtrls
NoCtrl == 0

\* The ring rotation is deterministic, so the round number alone names the entitled
\* controller; nothing has to be remembered about who held the token when.
HolderAt(r) == ((r - 1) % NumCtrls) + 1

VARIABLES round, view, bus, actor, atRound

vars == <<round, view, bus, actor, atRound>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ round \in 1..MaxRound
  /\ view \in [Ctrls -> 1..MaxRound]
  /\ bus \subseteq (Ctrls \X Bays \X (1..MaxRound))
  /\ actor \in [Bays -> Ctrls \cup {NoCtrl}]
  /\ atRound \in [Bays -> 0..MaxRound]

Init ==
  /\ round = 1
  /\ view = [c \in Ctrls |-> 1]
  /\ bus = {}
  /\ actor = [b \in Bays |-> NoCtrl]
  /\ atRound = [b \in Bays |-> 0]

\* Any controller may talk, entitled or not, and it stamps its own stale view.
IssueCommand(c, b) ==
  /\ ~\E m \in bus : m[1] = c
  /\ bus' = bus \cup {<<c, b, view[c]>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, view, actor, atRound>>

\* The bay checks entitlement against the round that is current at landing time,
\* which is what rejects a command that has aged out of its sender's round.
Deliver(c, b, r) ==
  /\ <<c, b, r>> \in bus
  /\ c = HolderAt(round)
  /\ r = round
  /\ actor' = [actor EXCEPT ![b] = c]
  /\ atRound' = [atRound EXCEPT ![b] = round]
  /\ bus' = bus \ {<<c, b, r>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, view>>

DiscardStale(c, b, r) ==
  /\ <<c, b, r>> \in bus
  /\ (c # HolderAt(round) \/ r # round)
  /\ bus' = bus \ {<<c, b, r>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, view, actor, atRound>>

Sync(c) ==
  /\ view[c] # round
  /\ view' = [view EXCEPT ![c] = round]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<round, bus, actor, atRound>>

PassToken ==
  /\ round < MaxRound
  /\ round' = round + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<view, bus, actor, atRound>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Ctrls, b \in Bays : IssueCommand(c, b)
  \/ \E c \in Ctrls, b \in Bays, r \in 1..MaxRound : Deliver(c, b, r) \/ DiscardStale(c, b, r)
  \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Sync(c)
  \/ PassToken

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every recorded bay action lines up with the entitlement the ring gave out.
ActionsWereEntitled ==
  \A b \in Bays : actor[b] # NoCtrl => actor[b] = HolderAt(atRound[b])

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumCtrls = 2
    Bays = {soap, rinse}
    MaxRound = 3
INVARIANT ActionsWereEntitled
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line has a ring of numbered line controllers that drive its treatment
bays -- the soap arch and the rinse arch -- and only one controller at a time is entitled
to command that hardware. Entitlement
circulates as a token around a fixed ring in a strictly deterministic rotation, and every
handover starts a new numbered round, so the round number by itself tells you which
controller is entitled during that round: round one belongs to the first controller in the
ring, round two to the second, and so on around and around.

Controllers learn about handovers by watching the line bus, and a controller's view of the
round number can lag behind reality. Worse, the bus is a mesh that reorders traffic: a
command a controller puts on the bus can sit there while several handovers go by and only
then reach the bay. So two bad things can reach a bay. One is a command from a controller
that was never entitled in the first place -- a desynchronised unit that wrongly believes
it is the current holder. The other is a command from a controller that genuinely was
entitled, but whose command has aged past the end of its round. The bay's defence is to
check, at the moment the command lands, that the round it is entitled to act in right now
is a round belonging to the sender: the bay stamps every action it performs with the round
that was current when it acted, together with the controller that caused it, and it
refuses anything that does not line up.

The full action set is: IssueCommand (any controller, entitled or not, puts a command for
a bay onto the reordering bus, stamped with that controller's possibly stale view of the
round), Deliver (a command lands at a bay while its sender is the controller entitled in
the round that is current right now, so the bay performs the action and records the causing
controller and the current round), DiscardStale (a command lands at a bay whose sender is
not the controller entitled in the current round, and the bay throws it away), Sync (a
controller refreshes its view of the round number), and PassToken (entitlement moves one
step around the ring and the round number advances).
SAFETY PROPERTY: for every bay action, the controller recorded as having caused it is the controller that the ring made entitled in the round recorded against that action, so no unentitled or time-expired controller ever moves a bay.

---- MODULE W4Od4m0p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Attendants, LineCap, MaxVersion

NoSnap == MaxVersion + 1

VARIABLES version, onLine, cleared, snapVer, snapOcc

vars == <<version, onLine, cleared, snapVer, snapOcc>>

\* Everything that has been committed against the line's capacity: vehicles already
\* on it, plus vehicles cleared onto the ramp that are still to roll on.
Committed == onLine + cleared

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
  /\ onLine \in 0..LineCap
  /\ cleared \in 0..LineCap
  /\ snapVer \in [Attendants -> 0..(MaxVersion + 1)]
  /\ snapOcc \in [Attendants -> 0..LineCap]

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ onLine = 0
  /\ cleared = 0
  /\ snapVer = [a \in Attendants |-> NoSnap]
  /\ snapOcc = [a \in Attendants |-> 0]

TakeSnapshot(a) ==
  /\ snapVer[a] = NoSnap
  /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![a] = version]
  /\ snapOcc' = [snapOcc EXCEPT ![a] = Committed]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, onLine, cleared>>

\* The attendant acts on the occupancy it read, not on a fresh reading; the version
\* match is what certifies that the old reading is still the truth.
CommitClear(a) ==
  /\ snapVer[a] # NoSnap
  /\ snapVer[a] = version
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ snapOcc[a] + 1 <= LineCap
  /\ cleared' = cleared + 1
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![a] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<onLine, snapOcc>>

Retry(a) ==
  /\ snapVer[a] # NoSnap
  /\ (snapVer[a] # version \/ snapOcc[a] + 1 > LineCap \/ version = MaxVersion)
  /\ snapVer' = [snapVer EXCEPT ![a] = NoSnap]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, onLine, cleared, snapOcc>>

RollOn ==
  /\ cleared > 0
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ cleared' = cleared - 1
  /\ onLine' = onLine + 1
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<snapVer, snapOcc>>

Exit ==
  /\ onLine > 0
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ onLine' = onLine - 1
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cleared, snapVer, snapOcc>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Attendants : TakeSnapshot(a) \/ CommitClear(a) \/ Retry(a)
  \/ RollOn
  \/ Exit

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A a \in Attendants : WF_vars(CommitClear(a) \/ Retry(a))

LineNotOverfilled == Committed <= LineCap

\* A slow attendant still always gets its snapshot resolved one way or the other.
SnapshotsResolve ==
  \A a \in Attendants : (snapVer[a] # NoSnap) ~> (snapVer[a] = NoSnap)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Attendants = {a1, a2}
    LineCap = 2
    MaxVersion = 4
INVARIANT LineNotOverfilled
PROPERTY SnapshotsResolve
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line can carry only so many vehicles between the entry gate and the
blower at the far end; past that number the cars touch and the line has to be stopped.
Vehicles are let on by gate attendants, and because the line is long the attendants work
optimistically rather than holding a gate lock. An attendant reads the line console, which
shows a version counter together with how many vehicles are on the line and how many have
been cleared onto the ramp but have not yet rolled on. It writes that pair down and then
walks back to its gate. Any change to the line -- a vehicle being cleared, a vehicle
rolling on, a vehicle leaving under the blower -- bumps the version counter.

An attendant can be slow. It is never removed from its post and it never abandons the
line, but an arbitrary amount of time can pass between reading the console and acting on
what it read, during which the line may have filled up behind its back. That is exactly
what the version counter is for: when the attendant finally tries to clear a vehicle, the
commit only goes through if the version it wrote down is still the live version, which
guarantees the occupancy figure it wrote down is still accurate and there is genuinely
room. If the version has moved, or the snapshot said there was no room, or the console has
run out of version numbers for this shift, the attendant tears up its snapshot and starts
over.

The full action set is: TakeSnapshot (an attendant records the current version together
with the occupancy it saw), CommitClear (an attendant whose snapshot version is still live
and whose snapshot showed headroom clears one vehicle onto the ramp and bumps the
version), Retry (an attendant whose snapshot is stale, showed no headroom, or cannot be
committed because the version counter is exhausted throws the snapshot away), RollOn (a
cleared vehicle actually rolls onto the line and bumps the version), and Exit (a vehicle
leaves the line under the blower and bumps the version).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the vehicles on the conveyor line plus the vehicles cleared onto the ramp but not yet rolled on never exceed the line's carrying capacity.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every snapshot an attendant takes is eventually disposed of, either by committing a clearance or by being torn up and retried.

---- MODULE W4Od12m0p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Techs, MaxUnits, MaxVersion

NoBadge == 0
NoNote == "none"
Notes == {NoNote} \cup ((0..MaxVersion) \X BOOLEAN)

VARIABLES version, note, stock, signedOut, badge, capacity

vars == <<version, note, stock, signedOut, badge, capacity>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
  /\ note \in [Techs -> Notes]
  /\ stock \in 0..MaxUnits
  /\ signedOut \in [Techs -> 0..MaxUnits]
  /\ badge \in [Techs -> 0..MaxUnits]
  /\ capacity \in 1..MaxUnits

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ note = [t \in Techs |-> NoNote]
  /\ stock = 0
  /\ signedOut = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
  /\ badge = [t \in Techs |-> NoBadge]
  /\ capacity = MaxUnits

\* A badge records the fridge configuration it was issued under, so a technician
\* carrying a badge from an earlier configuration counts as stale.
SignOnBadge(t) ==
  /\ badge[t] # capacity
  /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![t] = capacity]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, note, stock, signedOut, capacity>>

ReadRecord(t) ==
  /\ note[t] = NoNote
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![t] = <<version, stock > 0>>]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, stock, signedOut, badge, capacity>>

\* The version match certifies that the stale reading in the note is still true.
CommitSignOut(t) ==
  /\ note[t] # NoNote
  /\ note[t][1] = version
  /\ note[t][2]
  /\ badge[t] = capacity
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ stock' = stock - 1
  /\ signedOut' = [signedOut EXCEPT ![t] = signedOut[t] + 1]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![t] = NoNote]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<badge, capacity>>

TearUpNote(t) ==
  /\ note[t] # NoNote
  /\ (note[t][1] # version \/ ~note[t][2] \/ version = MaxVersion)
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![t] = NoNote]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, stock, signedOut, badge, capacity>>

ReturnUnit(t) ==
  /\ signedOut[t] > 0
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ signedOut' = [signedOut EXCEPT ![t] = signedOut[t] - 1]
  /\ stock' = stock + 1
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<note, badge, capacity>>

AcceptDonation ==
  /\ stock < capacity
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ stock' = stock + 1
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<note, signedOut, badge, capacity>>

\* Capacity changes only at a reconciled moment, and it retires every badge.
Reconfigure(c) ==
  /\ \A t \in Techs : signedOut[t] = 0
  /\ c # capacity
  /\ stock <= c
  /\ capacity' = c
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, note, stock, signedOut, badge>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Techs :
       SignOnBadge(t) \/ ReadRecord(t) \/ CommitSignOut(t) \/ TearUpNote(t) \/ ReturnUnit(t)
  \/ AcceptDonation
  \/ \E c \in 1..MaxUnits : Reconfigure(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

    MaxUnits = 2
    MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT StockOnlyWithCurrentBadge
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker guards the issue fridge. Technicians do not lock the
inventory record while they work; they read it optimistically. A technician glances at the
console, notes the record's version number and whether a spare unit was showing, and then
goes off to do something else. Any change to the inventory -- a unit signed out, a unit
returned, a donation added -- advances the version number, so when the technician finally
comes back to sign a unit out, the fridge only lets the sign-out through if the version it
noted is still the live one. That is what proves the reading it is acting on has not gone
stale. Otherwise the technician tears up the note and reads again.

Fridge capacity is not a constant. Shelves are taken out and brought back into use as
chillers are serviced, so the number of units the fridge may hold is reconfigured while
the tracker is running, and reconfiguration is only permitted when nothing is signed out,
so that the count on the floor always reconciles. Reconfiguration is also the moment
credentials are re-issued: a technician's badge records the fridge configuration it was
issued against. A technician who has never been badged is simply unauthorised, and a
technician still carrying a badge from the previous configuration is stale; neither is
permitted to sign a unit out, and both must present themselves for a fresh badge first.

The full action set is: SignOnBadge (a technician takes a badge stamped with the fridge's
current configuration), ReadRecord (a technician notes the record's version and whether a
spare unit was showing), CommitSignOut (a technician with a current badge and a note whose
version is still live signs one unit out, which advances the version), TearUpNote (a
technician whose note is stale, whose note showed no spare unit, or who finds the version
counter exhausted for the shift, discards the note), ReturnUnit (a technician brings a
signed-out unit back, which advances the version), AcceptDonation (a new unit is added
while the fridge is under its configured capacity, which advances the version), and
Reconfigure (the fridge's capacity is changed while nothing is signed out, which
invalidates every badge issued against the previous configuration).
SAFETY PROPERTY: no technician ever has a unit signed out to them unless their badge is stamped with the fridge's current configuration, so neither an unbadged nor a stale-badged technician ever holds stock.

---- MODULE W4Od11m1p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumStations

Stations == 1..NumStations
Around(i) == IF i = NumStations THEN 1 ELSE i + 1

VARIABLES token, pending, carded, driving, rack

vars == <<token, pending, carded, driving, rack>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ token \in Stations
  /\ pending \subseteq Stations
  /\ carded \subseteq Stations
  /\ driving \subseteq Stations
  /\ rack \subseteq Stations

Init ==
  /\ token = 1
  /\ pending = {}
  /\ carded = {}
  /\ driving = {}
  /\ rack = {}

SubmitJob(i) ==
  /\ i \notin pending
  /\ i \notin carded
  /\ i \notin rack
  /\ pending' = pending \cup {i}
  /\ rack' = rack \cup {i}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, carded, driving>>

\* The rack is a bag, not a queue: cards come out in an arbitrary order.
PickUpCard(i) ==
  /\ i \in rack
  /\ rack' = rack \ {i}
  /\ carded' = carded \cup {i}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pending, driving>>

\* Driving the imagesetter is conditioned on holding the dispatch token.
StartPlate(i) ==
  /\ token = i
  /\ i \in pending
  /\ i \in carded
  /\ i \notin driving
  /\ driving' = driving \cup {i}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, pending, carded, rack>>

FinishPlate(i) ==
  /\ i \in driving
  /\ driving' = driving \ {i}
  /\ pending' = pending \ {i}
  /\ carded' = carded \ {i}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, rack>>

\* The turn is not given up while the holder still owes a plate.
PassToken ==
  /\ token \notin pending
  /\ token' = Around(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, carded, driving, rack>>

Next ==
  \/ \E i \in Stations : SubmitJob(i) \/ PickUpCard(i) \/ StartPlate(i) \/ FinishPlate(i)
  \/ PassToken

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(PassToken)
  /\ \A i \in Stations : WF_vars(PickUpCard(i))
  /\ \A i \in Stations : SF_vars(StartPlate(i))
  /\ \A i \in Stations : WF_vars(FinishPlate(i))

\* Whoever is on the imagesetter can only be the current token holder.
ImagesetterHeldByTokenOnly == driving \subseteq {token}

EveryJobReachesThePlate ==
  \A i \in Stations : (i \in pending) ~> (i \in driving)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumStations = 3
INVARIANT ImagesetterHeldByTokenOnly
PROPERTY EveryJobReachesThePlate
nl:
A print shop job spooler feeds one imagesetter, and the imagesetter is the critical
resource: it exposes one plate at a time and nothing else may drive it while a plate is on
it. The workstations that submit jobs are arranged in a ring, and a single dispatch token
travels around that ring in fixed order. A workstation may only put a plate on the
imagesetter while the token is sitting with it.

Job submissions do not travel with the token. A workstation announces a job by dropping a
request card into the shop's pigeonhole rack, and the rack is emptied in whatever order
the spooler clerk happens to pick cards out, so a card dropped earlier can easily be
picked up later than one dropped afterwards. The spooler will not start a plate for a
workstation until that workstation's card has actually been picked up, so a workstation
whose card is still sitting in the rack simply keeps hold of the token and waits. That is
also why the token is never handed on while its holder still has an outstanding job: the
turn belongs to that workstation until its plate has been exposed.

The full action set is: SubmitJob (a workstation takes on a job and drops its request card
into the pigeonhole rack), PickUpCard (the clerk picks some card out of the rack, in no
particular order, and registers that job with the spooler), StartPlate (the workstation
that holds the token, and whose card has been picked up, puts its plate on the
imagesetter), FinishPlate (the plate is exposed, the imagesetter is released and the job is
done), and PassToken (a workstation with no outstanding job hands the dispatch token to
the next workstation around the ring).
SAFETY PROPERTY: a workstation has a plate on the imagesetter only while it is the one holding the dispatch token, so two workstations can never be driving the imagesetter at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every workstation that takes on a job eventually gets its plate onto the imagesetter.

---- MODULE W4Od16m4p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Pharmacists, Chief, SpoolLimit, MaxRevision

NoCred == 0

VARIABLES spool, cred, revision, dispensed

vars == <<spool, cred, revision, dispensed>>

\* A credential is only current if it carries the revision now in force; an older
\* stamp is stale and counts for no more than never having been credentialed.
Current(p) == cred[p] = revision

Spools == UNION {[1..n -> Pharmacists] : n \in 0..(SpoolLimit + 1)}

TypeOK ==
  /\ spool \in Spools
  /\ cred \in [Pharmacists -> 0..MaxRevision]
  /\ revision \in 1..MaxRevision
  /\ dispensed \in 0..SpoolLimit

Init ==
  /\ spool = << >>
  /\ cred = [p \in Pharmacists |-> NoCred]
  /\ revision = 1
  /\ dispensed = 0

Credential(p) ==
  /\ ~Current(p)
  /\ cred' = [cred EXCEPT ![p] = revision]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, revision, dispensed>>

\* A credential cannot be pulled while that pharmacist still has work spooled.
Withdraw(p) ==
  /\ cred[p] # NoCred
  /\ \A i \in 1..Len(spool) : spool[i] # p
  /\ cred' = [cred EXCEPT ![p] = NoCred]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, revision, dispensed>>

\* Backpressure: ordinary lodgement stops at the spool limit.
Lodge(p) ==
  /\ Current(p)
  /\ Len(spool) < SpoolLimit
  /\ spool' = Append(spool, p)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, revision, dispensed>>

\* The privileged override buys one reserved slot past the limit, nothing more.
EmergencyLodge ==
  /\ Current(Chief)
  /\ Len(spool) < SpoolLimit + 1
  /\ spool' = Append(spool, Chief)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, revision, dispensed>>

Dispense ==
  /\ Len(spool) > 0
  /\ dispensed < SpoolLimit
  /\ spool' = Tail(spool)
  /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<cred, revision>>

Collect ==
  /\ dispensed > 0
  /\ dispensed' = dispensed - 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, cred, revision>>

\* Revising the formulary strands nothing, because the spool is drained first.
Revise ==
  /\ revision < MaxRevision
  /\ spool = << >>
  /\ revision' = revision + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, cred, dispensed>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Pharmacists : Credential(p) \/ Withdraw(p) \/ Lodge(p)
  \/ EmergencyLodge
  \/ Dispense
  \/ Collect
  \/ Revise

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SpooledWorkIsCredentialed ==
  \A i \in 1..Len(spool) : cred[spool[i]] = revision

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Pharmacists = {locum, chief}
    Chief = chief
    SpoolLimit = 2
    MaxRevision = 3
INVARIANT SpooledWorkIsCredentialed
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser takes work through a bounded spool. Prescriptions queue
up in the order they are lodged, the spool holds only a set number of them, and when it is
full the counter simply refuses new work -- backpressure, so the robot is never asked to
hold more than it can track. Every queued item is lodged on behalf of a named pharmacist.

Who may lodge work is governed by the formulary revision in force. A pharmacist's
dispensing credential is stamped with the revision it was granted under. When the
formulary is revised, every credential stamped with the old revision becomes stale, and a
pharmacist carrying a stale credential is as barred from lodging or dispensing work as one
who was never credentialed at all; they must be re-credentialed against the new revision
first. Because a revision would strand any work already lodged under the old rules, the
formulary is only revised when the spool has been drained empty. In the same spirit, a
credential is only withdrawn from a pharmacist who has no work sitting in the spool.

The superintendent pharmacist has one privilege the others do not: an emergency lodgement
that goes into a reserved slot beyond the ordinary spool limit, so a genuinely urgent
prescription is not turned away by backpressure. The privilege buys a way past the
backpressure only -- the superintendent still needs a credential stamped with the current
revision like everyone else.

The full action set is: Credential (a pharmacist is granted a credential stamped with the
formulary revision now in force), Withdraw (a credential is taken away from a pharmacist
who has nothing in the spool), Lodge (a currently credentialed pharmacist adds a
prescription to the back of the spool, provided the spool is below its ordinary limit),
EmergencyLodge (the superintendent, currently credentialed, adds an urgent prescription
using the reserved slot beyond the ordinary limit), Dispense (the robot takes the
prescription at the head of the spool and makes it up onto the collection shelf), Collect
(a patient takes a made-up prescription off the collection shelf), and Revise (the formulary
revision is advanced while the spool is empty, retiring every credential stamped with the
previous revision).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every prescription sitting in the spool belongs to a pharmacist whose credential is stamped with the formulary revision currently in force.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m0p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Drones, Cards, MaxVersion

NoRead == <<MaxVersion + 1, 0>>
Readings == (0..(MaxVersion + 1)) \X (0..Cards)

VARIABLES version, reading, pool, booked, flying, silent

vars == <<version, reading, pool, booked, flying, silent>>

RECURSIVE SumOf(_, _)
SumOf(f, S) ==
  IF S = {} THEN 0
  ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOf(f, S \ {x})

\* A card is always in exactly one of three places: the pool, a booking, or the air.
Accounted == pool + SumOf(booked, Drones) + SumOf(flying, Drones)

TypeOK ==
  /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
  /\ reading \in [Drones -> Readings]
  /\ pool \in 0..Cards
  /\ booked \in [Drones -> 0..Cards]
  /\ flying \in [Drones -> 0..Cards]
  /\ silent \in [Drones -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
  /\ version = 0
  /\ reading = [d \in Drones |-> NoRead]
  /\ pool = Cards
  /\ booked = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ flying = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
  /\ silent = [d \in Drones |-> FALSE]

ReadBoard(d) ==
  /\ ~silent[d]
  /\ reading[d] = NoRead
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![d] = <<version, pool>>]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pool, booked, flying, silent>>

\* The version match certifies that the pool count the drone noted is still true.
BookOut(d) ==
  /\ reading[d] # NoRead
  /\ reading[d][1] = version
  /\ reading[d][2] > 0
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ pool' = pool - 1
  /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![d] = booked[d] + 1]
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![d] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<flying, silent>>

Discard(d) ==
  /\ ~silent[d]
  /\ reading[d] # NoRead
  /\ (reading[d][1] # version \/ reading[d][2] = 0 \/ version = MaxVersion)
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![d] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pool, booked, flying, silent>>

\* The ground station cannot tell a silent drone from a busy one, so it may give up
\* on any outstanding reading; abandoning one moves no card.
Abandon(d) ==
  /\ reading[d] # NoRead
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![d] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, pool, booked, flying, silent>>

TakeUp(d) ==
  /\ ~silent[d]
  /\ booked[d] > 0
  /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![d] = booked[d] - 1]
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![d] = flying[d] + 1]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, reading, pool, silent>>

HandBack(d) ==
  /\ ~silent[d]
  /\ flying[d] > 0
  /\ version < MaxVersion
  /\ flying' = [flying EXCEPT ![d] = flying[d] - 1]
  /\ pool' = pool + 1
  /\ version' = version + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, booked, silent>>

GoSilent(d) ==
  /\ \A e \in Drones : ~silent[e]
  /\ silent' = [silent EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<version, reading, pool, booked, flying>>

Next ==
  \E d \in Drones :
    ReadBoard(d) \/ BookOut(d) \/ Discard(d) \/ Abandon(d)
      \/ TakeUp(d) \/ HandBack(d) \/ GoSilent(d)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A d \in Drones : WF_vars(BookOut(d) \/ Discard(d) \/ Abandon(d))

CardsAreConserved == Accounted = Cards

ReadingsClear ==
  \A d \in Drones : (reading[d] # NoRead) ~> (reading[d] = NoRead)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {d1, d2}
    Cards = 2
    MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT CardsAreConserved
PROPERTY ReadingsClear
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm divides the fire perimeter into a fixed set of survey
sectors. There are exactly as many sector cards as there are sectors, and the swarm's
whole point is that a card is never duplicated and never mislaid: at any instant every
card is either sitting unassigned in the ground station's pool, or booked out to a drone
and awaiting handover, or actually flown by a drone. Nothing else can happen to a card.

Drones take work optimistically instead of holding the assignment board. A drone reads the
board, noting its version number and how many cards were in the pool, and then flies on.
Any movement of a card advances the board's version, so when the drone finally tries to
book a card out, the ground station lets it through only if the version the drone noted is
still the live one -- proof that the pool count it read is still true. Otherwise the drone
discards its reading and reads the board again later.

Any one drone in the swarm may go silent without warning: the radio fails and it stops
answering, though the ground station has no way to distinguish that from a drone that is
simply busy. So the ground station will not wait indefinitely for an outstanding reading
to be acted on; it may abandon any reading it is still waiting on, which returns the drone
to a clean slate without moving any card.

The full action set is: ReadBoard (a drone notes the board version and the pool count),
BookOut (a drone whose noted version is still live and who saw a card in the pool moves one
card from the pool into its own booking, advancing the version), Discard (a drone whose
reading is stale, who saw an empty pool, or who finds the board's version counter used up
tears up its reading), Abandon (the ground station gives up on an outstanding reading it is
still waiting on), TakeUp (a drone that is still answering converts its booking into a card
it is actually flying), HandBack (a drone that is still answering returns a card it was
flying to the pool, advancing the version), and GoSilent (the one drone that can fail
silently loses its radio).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the cards in the ground station's pool, the cards booked out to drones and the cards being flown always add up to exactly the number of sector cards the swarm started with.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every reading a drone takes off the board is eventually cleared, whether by booking a card out, by the drone tearing it up, or by the ground station abandoning it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m0p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Controllers, NumRunways, MaxStrips

Runways == 1..NumRunways

NoNote == MaxStrips + 1
NoReceipt == 0
Boards == UNION {[1..n -> Runways] : n \in 0..MaxStrips}

VARIABLES board, note, rcptAt, rcptRwy, open

vars == <<board, note, rcptAt, rcptRwy, open>>

\* A strip is pinned once some controller has been given a receipt for its position.
Receipted(i) == \E c \in Controllers : rcptAt[c] = i

TypeOK ==
  /\ board \in Boards
  /\ note \in [Controllers -> 0..(MaxStrips + 1)]
  /\ rcptAt \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxStrips]
  /\ rcptRwy \in [Controllers -> Runways \cup {NoReceipt}]
  /\ open \subseteq Runways

Init ==
  /\ board = << >>
  /\ note = [c \in Controllers |-> NoNote]
  /\ rcptAt = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
  /\ rcptRwy = [c \in Controllers |-> NoReceipt]
  /\ open = Runways

ReadBoard(c) ==
  /\ note[c] = NoNote
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![c] = Len(board)]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, rcptAt, rcptRwy, open>>

\* The length match is the compare half of the compare-and-append.
AddStrip(c, r) ==
  /\ note[c] # NoNote
  /\ note[c] = Len(board)
  /\ Len(board) < MaxStrips
  /\ r \in open
  /\ board' = Append(board, r)
  /\ rcptAt' = [rcptAt EXCEPT ![c] = Len(board) + 1]
  /\ rcptRwy' = [rcptRwy EXCEPT ![c] = r]
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![c] = NoNote]
  /\ UNCHANGED open

TearUp(c) ==
  /\ note[c] # NoNote
  /\ (note[c] # Len(board) \/ Len(board) = MaxStrips)
  /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![c] = NoNote]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, rcptAt, rcptRwy, open>>

\* Capacity moves at runtime, but replanning may not touch a receipted strip.
Rewrite(i, r) ==
  /\ i \in 1..Len(board)
  /\ ~Receipted(i)
  /\ r \in open
  /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![i] = r]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<note, rcptAt, rcptRwy, open>>

CutBack(k) ==
  /\ k < Len(board)
  /\ \A c \in Controllers : rcptAt[c] <= k
  /\ board' = SubSeq(board, 1, k)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<note, rcptAt, rcptRwy, open>>

CloseRunway(r) ==
  /\ r \in open
  /\ open' = open \ {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, note, rcptAt, rcptRwy>>

OpenRunway(r) ==
  /\ r \notin open
  /\ open' = open \cup {r}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, note, rcptAt, rcptRwy>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Controllers : ReadBoard(c) \/ TearUp(c)
  \/ \E c \in Controllers, r \in Runways : AddStrip(c, r)
  \/ \E i \in 1..MaxStrips, r \in Runways : Rewrite(i, r)
  \/ \E k \in 0..MaxStrips : CutBack(k)
  \/ \E r \in Runways : CloseRunway(r) \/ OpenRunway(r)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ReceiptsStillHold ==
  \A c \in Controllers :
    rcptAt[c] # 0 => (rcptAt[c] \in 1..Len(board) /\ board[rcptAt[c]] = rcptRwy[c])

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    NumRunways = 2
    MaxStrips = 2
INVARIANT ReceiptsStillHold
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator keeps one shared record of the departure order: an
append-only strip board, where each strip in turn names the runway a departure has been
given. Controllers do not lock the board. A controller reads how many strips are currently
on it, thinks about the traffic, and only then tries to add a strip. The add goes through
only if the board is still exactly the length it was when the controller read it; if
somebody else has added a strip in the meantime the controller's reasoning is out of date,
so it tears up its intention and reads the board again. That check is the whole defence
against one controller's addition quietly overwriting another's.

When a strip is accepted the controller is given a receipt: the position its strip landed
at and the runway written on it. A receipt is a promise about the shared record, and the
allocator must honour it.

Runway capacity moves around during the day. Runways are closed for a rubber sweep or a
crosswind and reopened later, so the set of usable runways changes underneath a board that
already has strips on it. The allocator deals with that in two ways. It may rewrite a
strip that names a runway which has since closed, moving that departure to a runway that
is open; and it may cut the board back to a shorter prefix when the tail of the plan has
become unflyable. Both are only permitted on strips that no controller has been given a
receipt for -- a receipted strip may be neither rewritten nor cut away.

The full action set is: ReadBoard (a controller notes the current length of the strip
board), AddStrip (a controller whose noted length still matches the board appends a strip
naming an open runway and is given a receipt for its position and runway), TearUp (a
controller whose noted length no longer matches the board, or who finds the board already
at its maximum length, abandons the attempt), Rewrite (a strip nobody has a receipt for is
changed to name a different open runway), CutBack (the board is cut back to a prefix,
provided no receipted strip would be lost), CloseRunway (a runway stops being usable), and
OpenRunway (a runway becomes usable again).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every receipt a controller holds still names a position that exists on the strip board and carries exactly the runway the receipt promised.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m0p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Operators, NumSlots, MaxOverrides

Slots == 1..NumSlots
Nobody == "free"
NoLook == {0}

VARIABLES board, docket, look, overrides

vars == <<board, docket, look, overrides>>

FreeSlots == {s \in Slots : board[s] = Nobody}

TypeOK ==
  /\ board \in [Slots -> Operators \cup {Nobody}]
  /\ docket \in [Operators -> SUBSET Slots]
  /\ look \in [Operators -> SUBSET (0..NumSlots)]
  /\ overrides \in 0..MaxOverrides

Init ==
  /\ board = [s \in Slots |-> Nobody]
  /\ docket = [o \in Operators |-> {}]
  /\ look = [o \in Operators |-> NoLook]
  /\ overrides = 0

ReadTheBoard(o) ==
  /\ look[o] = NoLook
  /\ look' = [look EXCEPT ![o] = FreeSlots]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, docket, overrides>>

\* The memorised free set must still be the board's free set: an unchanged board
\* is what makes the operator's stale picture safe to act on.
TakeSlot(o, s) ==
  /\ look[o] # NoLook
  /\ look[o] = FreeSlots
  /\ s \in look[o]
  /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![s] = o]
  /\ look' = [look EXCEPT ![o] = NoLook]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<docket, overrides>>

LookAgain(o) ==
  /\ look[o] # NoLook
  /\ (look[o] # FreeSlots \/ look[o] = {})
  /\ look' = [look EXCEPT ![o] = NoLook]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, docket, overrides>>

\* Copying into the docket lags the board, which is where an override can bite.
WriteDocket(o, s) ==
  /\ board[s] = o
  /\ s \notin docket[o]
  /\ docket' = [docket EXCEPT ![o] = docket[o] \cup {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<board, look, overrides>>

ReleaseSlot(o, s) ==
  /\ board[s] = o
  /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![s] = Nobody]
  /\ docket' = [docket EXCEPT ![o] = docket[o] \ {s}]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<look, overrides>>

\* The override must strike the slot from the old holder's docket as it moves it.
ManagerOverride(o, s) ==
  /\ overrides < MaxOverrides
  /\ board[s] # o
  /\ board' = [board EXCEPT ![s] = o]
  /\ docket' = [p \in Operators |-> IF p = o THEN docket[p] ELSE docket[p] \ {s}]
  /\ overrides' = overrides + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED look

Next ==
  \/ \E o \in Operators : ReadTheBoard(o) \/ LookAgain(o)
  \/ \E o \in Operators, s \in Slots :
       TakeSlot(o, s) \/ WriteDocket(o, s) \/ ReleaseSlot(o, s) \/ ManagerOverride(o, s)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A o \in Operators, s \in Slots : WF_vars(ReleaseSlot(o, s))

DocketsBackedByBoard ==
  \A o \in Operators : docket[o] \subseteq {s \in Slots : board[s] = o}

BookedSlotsAreFreedAgain ==
  \A s \in Slots : (board[s] # Nobody) ~> (board[s] = Nobody)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Operators = {o1, o2}
    NumSlots = 2
    MaxOverrides = 2
INVARIANT DocketsBackedByBoard
PROPERTY BookedSlotsAreFreedAgain
nl:
A print shop job spooler hands out press slots -- the numbered windows in the day's press
schedule. The shop keeps one slot board on the wall, and operators do not lock it while
they think. An operator glances at the board, memorises which slots are showing free,
walks back to its press, and only then tries to take one. The take is accepted only if the
board still shows exactly the free slots the operator memorised; if anything on the board
has moved in the meantime, the memorised picture is worthless and the operator has to look
again. Because the board itself is what records who has which slot, and because the take
is only accepted against an unchanged board, the same slot cannot end up written against
two operators.

Taking a slot on the board and writing it into your own press docket are separate steps,
and there is a gap between them. That gap is where the shop manager's privilege bites. The
manager may override the board and force a slot across to a different operator, and the
rule is that the override must strike the slot out of the previous holder's docket in the
same movement: an entry in a docket that the board no longer backs would send two presses
after the same window. The manager's privilege is rationed to a handful of uses per shift,
so it cannot be used to keep a slot in play forever.

The full action set is: ReadTheBoard (an operator memorises the set of slots currently
showing free), TakeSlot (an operator whose memorised picture still matches the board takes
one of the slots it saw free, and the board is written up in that operator's name),
LookAgain (an operator whose memorised picture no longer matches the board, or who saw
nothing free, throws the picture away), WriteDocket (an operator whose name is on the board
against a slot copies that slot into its own press docket), ReleaseSlot (an operator
finishes with a slot and clears it from both the board and its docket), and
ManagerOverride (the shop manager forces a slot across to a nominated operator, striking
it out of the previous holder's docket as part of the same movement, and using up one of
the shift's rationed overrides).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every slot written in an operator's press docket is a slot the wall board currently records against that same operator, so no slot is ever allocated to two operators at once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every slot that gets written up on the board is eventually cleared from it again.
