---- MODULE W4Od0m7p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Planners, NumTheatres, Sessions, MaxClosed

Theatres == 1..NumTheatres

\* Theatres are not staffed alike: the odd-numbered ones run a full list, the
\* even-numbered ones lose a session to their shared recovery bay.
Staffed(t) == Sessions - ((t - 1) % 2)

NoCopy == [t \in Theatres |-> Sessions + 1]

VARIABLES booked, copy, waiting, closed

vars == <<booked, copy, waiting, closed>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ booked \in [Theatres -> 0..Sessions]
  /\ copy \in [Planners -> [Theatres -> 0..(Sessions + 1)]]
  /\ waiting \in [Planners -> BOOLEAN]
  /\ closed \in 0..MaxClosed

Init ==
  /\ booked = [t \in Theatres |-> 0]
  /\ copy = [p \in Planners |-> NoCopy]
  /\ waiting = [p \in Planners |-> FALSE]
  /\ closed = 0

PatientArrives(p) ==
  /\ ~waiting[p]
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![p] = TRUE]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, copy, closed>>

CopyRegister(p) ==
  /\ waiting[p]
  /\ copy[p] = NoCopy
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![p] = booked]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, waiting, closed>>

\* The compare covers the whole register, so a decision reasoned from a copy that
\* has since been overtaken cannot be swapped in.
CommitSession(p, t) ==
  /\ copy[p] # NoCopy
  /\ copy[p] = booked
  /\ copy[p][t] < Staffed(t)
  /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![t] = booked[t] + 1]
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![p] = NoCopy]
  /\ waiting' = [waiting EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE]
  /\ UNCHANGED closed

StartOver(p) ==
  /\ copy[p] # NoCopy
  /\ (copy[p] # booked \/ \A t \in Theatres : copy[p][t] >= Staffed(t))
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![p] = NoCopy]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<booked, waiting, closed>>

CloseCase(t) ==
  /\ booked[t] > 0
  /\ closed < MaxClosed
  /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![t] = booked[t] - 1]
  /\ closed' = closed + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<copy, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E p \in Planners : PatientArrives(p) \/ CopyRegister(p) \/ StartOver(p)
  \/ \E p \in Planners, t \in Theatres : CommitSession(p, t)
  \/ \E t \in Theatres : CloseCase(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoTheatreOverbooked ==
  \A t \in Theatres : booked[t] <= Staffed(t)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Planners = {p1, p2}
    NumTheatres = 2
    Sessions = 2
    MaxClosed = 2
INVARIANT NoTheatreOverbooked
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler protects one shared booking register. The register
holds, for every theatre, how many sessions of the day have already been committed to it,
and no theatre may be committed beyond the number of sessions its staff can actually
cover. That number is not the same everywhere: the theatres that share the recovery bay
run one session fewer than the rest. Planners update the register with a compare-and-swap: a planner takes a complete
copy of the register, works out from that copy whether the theatre it has a patient for
still has a session spare, and then swaps its decision in. The swap is accepted only if
the register is still, in every entry, identical to the copy the planner took. If anything
has moved, the copy the planner reasoned from was out of date and the whole attempt is
thrown away and started again.

Planners can be slow. A planner is never taken off the rota and never abandons a patient,
but an arbitrary amount of time may pass between taking its copy of the register and
trying to swap its decision in -- a ward round, a delayed transfer, a conversation with a
surgeon. During that gap other planners commit sessions, which is exactly why the
comparison covers the whole register and not just the entry being changed: a decision
reasoned from a stale copy must never be allowed through.

The full action set is: PatientArrives (a planner picks up a patient who needs theatre
time), CopyRegister (a planner with a patient takes a complete copy of the booking
register), CommitSession (a planner whose copy still matches the register in every entry,
and whose copy showed the chosen theatre with a session to spare, commits one session to
that theatre), StartOver (a planner whose copy no longer matches the register, or whose
copy showed no theatre with a session to spare, throws the copy away), and CloseCase (a
committed session is completed and released back to its theatre).
SAFETY PROPERTY: no theatre is ever committed to more sessions than its staff can cover.

---- MODULE W4Od10m5p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumNodes, Quorum, MaxBallot

Nodes == 1..NumNodes
NoNode == 0

VARIABLES phase, ballot, vote, roster, backers, silent

vars == <<phase, ballot, vote, roster, backers, silent>>

\* A vote only counts if it is stamped with the ballot now running and comes from a
\* node that is currently on the roster.
LiveVoters == {n \in roster : vote[n] = ballot}
Answering == {n \in roster : n # silent}

TypeOK ==
  /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
  /\ ballot \in 0..MaxBallot
  /\ vote \in [Nodes -> 0..MaxBallot]
  /\ roster \subseteq Nodes
  /\ backers \subseteq Nodes
  /\ silent \in Nodes \cup {NoNode}

Init ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ ballot = 0
  /\ vote = [n \in Nodes |-> 0]
  /\ roster = Nodes
  /\ backers = {}
  /\ silent = NoNode

OpenBallot ==
  /\ phase = "idle"
  /\ backers = {}
  /\ ballot < MaxBallot
  /\ ballot' = ballot + 1
  /\ phase' = "voting"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<vote, roster, backers, silent>>

CastVote(n) ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ n \in roster
  /\ n # silent
  /\ vote[n] # ballot
  /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![n] = ballot]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, roster, backers, silent>>

Grant ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ Cardinality(LiveVoters) >= Quorum
  /\ backers' = LiveVoters
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, vote, roster, silent>>

Abandon ==
  /\ phase = "voting"
  /\ Cardinality(Answering) < Quorum
  /\ phase' = "idle"
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, vote, roster, backers, silent>>

Release ==
  /\ backers # {}
  /\ backers' = {}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, vote, roster, silent>>

\* Taking a node off the roster may not undermine an outstanding grant.
Decommission(n) ==
  /\ n \in roster
  /\ Cardinality(backers \cap (roster \ {n})) >= Quorum \/ backers = {}
  /\ roster' = roster \ {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, vote, backers, silent>>

Recommission(n) ==
  /\ n \notin roster
  /\ roster' = roster \cup {n}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, vote, backers, silent>>

GoSilent(n) ==
  /\ silent = NoNode
  /\ silent' = n
  /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, ballot, vote, roster, backers>>

Next ==
  \/ OpenBallot \/ Grant \/ Abandon \/ Release
  \/ \E n \in Nodes : CastVote(n) \/ Decommission(n) \/ Recommission(n) \/ GoSilent(n)

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A n \in Nodes : SF_vars(CastVote(n))
  /\ SF_vars(Grant \/ Abandon)

GrantsKeepAQuorum ==
  backers # {} => Cardinality(backers \cap roster) >= Quorum

BallotsDecide ==
  (phase = "voting") ~> (phase = "idle")

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumNodes = 3
    Quorum = 2
    MaxBallot = 2
INVARIANT GrantsKeepAQuorum
PROPERTY BallotsDecide
nl:
A subway signalling block system does not let any single interlocking node hand a train
movement authority for a block. Authority is granted only when a quorum of the nodes on
the current signalling roster votes for it, and voting happens in numbered ballots. Every
vote a node casts is stamped with the ballot it was cast in, so a vote left over from an
earlier ballot carries no weight in the current one; and a node that is not on the roster
has no standing to vote at all. Between them those two rules mean that neither a node
whose authorisation has been taken away nor a node still repeating an old ballot's answer
can move a train.

Exactly one node in the system may fail silently. Its radio simply stops and it casts no
more votes, but nobody can tell whether it has failed or is merely busy, so it is left on
the roster and the quorum is sized so that the remaining nodes can still reach a decision
without it. Roster changes are a separate, deliberate matter: a node may be taken off the
roster only when doing so would still leave any outstanding grant backed by a quorum of
rostered nodes, and it can be put back on later.

The full action set is: OpenBallot (the system opens a new numbered ballot for a block,
which can only happen when no grant is outstanding), CastVote (a rostered node that has
not gone silent casts its vote, stamped with the current ballot), Grant (a quorum of
rostered nodes has voted in the current ballot, so movement authority is granted and the
voters who backed it are recorded), Abandon (too few rostered nodes are still answering to
reach a quorum, so the ballot is dropped), Release (the train clears the block and the
grant is given up), Decommission (a node is taken off the roster, permitted only when any
outstanding grant would still hold a quorum without it), Recommission (a node is put back
on the roster), and GoSilent (the one node that can fail silently loses its radio).
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever movement authority is outstanding, the nodes recorded as having voted for it still include a quorum of nodes on the current roster.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every ballot that is opened eventually reaches a decision, either granting movement authority or being abandoned.

---- MODULE W4Od4m4p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS NumTerminals, SpoolLimit, MaxRevision

Terminals == 1..NumTerminals
Tickets == Terminals \X (1..MaxRevision)
NoWash == <<0, 0>>
NoTerminal == 0
Spools == UNION {[1..n -> Tickets] : n \in 0..SpoolLimit}

VARIABLES spool, revision, commissioned, running, silent

vars == <<spool, revision, commissioned, running, silent>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ spool \in Spools
  /\ revision \in 1..MaxRevision
  /\ commissioned \subseteq Terminals
  /\ running \in Tickets \cup {NoWash}
  /\ silent \in Terminals \cup {NoTerminal}

Init ==
  /\ spool = << >>
  /\ revision = 1
  /\ commissioned = Terminals
  /\ running = NoWash
  /\ silent = NoTerminal

\* Backpressure: the spool refuses work once it is at its limit.
LodgeTicket(t) ==
  /\ t \in commissioned
  /\ t # silent
  /\ Len(spool) < SpoolLimit
  /\ spool' = Append(spool, <<t, revision>>)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, commissioned, running, silent>>

\* Both disqualifications are re-checked as the ticket comes off the spool.
StartWash ==
  /\ Len(spool) > 0
  /\ running = NoWash
  /\ Head(spool)[1] \in commissioned
  /\ Head(spool)[2] = revision
  /\ running' = Head(spool)
  /\ spool' = Tail(spool)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, commissioned, silent>>

DropTicket ==
  /\ Len(spool) > 0
  /\ (Head(spool)[1] \notin commissioned \/ Head(spool)[2] # revision)
  /\ spool' = Tail(spool)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, commissioned, running, silent>>

FinishWash ==
  /\ running # NoWash
  /\ running' = NoWash
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, revision, commissioned, silent>>

\* Programmes change between washes, never underneath one.
ReviseProgramme ==
  /\ running = NoWash
  /\ revision < MaxRevision
  /\ revision' = revision + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, commissioned, running, silent>>

Commission(t) ==
  /\ t \notin commissioned
  /\ commissioned' = commissioned \cup {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, revision, running, silent>>

Decommission(t) ==
  /\ t \in commissioned
  /\ running[1] # t
  /\ commissioned' = commissioned \ {t}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, revision, running, silent>>

GoSilent(t) ==
  /\ silent = NoTerminal
  /\ silent' = t
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, revision, commissioned, running>>

Next ==
  \/ \E t \in Terminals : LodgeTicket(t) \/ Commission(t) \/ Decommission(t) \/ GoSilent(t)
  \/ StartWash \/ DropTicket \/ FinishWash \/ ReviseProgramme

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

RunningWashIsEntitled ==
  running \in {NoWash} \cup (commissioned \X {revision})

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumTerminals = 2
    SpoolLimit = 2
    MaxRevision = 2
INVARIANT RunningWashIsEntitled
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line takes its work from a bounded spool. Attendant terminals lodge
wash tickets into the spool, the spool holds only so many tickets, and when it is full the
terminals are simply refused -- backpressure, so nothing is accepted that the tunnel
cannot track. Each ticket records which terminal lodged it and which revision of the wash
programme was in force at the moment of lodging.

Two things disqualify a ticket from actually driving the tunnel. A terminal may have been
decommissioned since it lodged its ticket -- taken out of the till system, no longer a
party to anything -- in which case it has no standing to start a wash. Or the wash
programme may have been revised since the ticket was lodged, in which case the ticket
describes a wash the tunnel no longer offers and is stale. The tunnel therefore re-checks
both facts as it takes each ticket off the front of the spool, and throws away any ticket
that fails either check rather than running it. Two matching rules keep the running wash
honest: a terminal cannot be decommissioned while its ticket is the one the tunnel is
actually running, and the wash programme is only revised between washes, never while the
tunnel is mid-cycle.

One terminal in the shop can fail silently: its till link dies and it stops lodging
anything more, but nobody notices and it is left commissioned, so tickets it lodged before
the failure sit in the spool and remain perfectly valid work.

The full action set is: LodgeTicket (a commissioned terminal that has not failed lodges a
ticket stamped with the current programme revision, provided the spool is below its
limit), StartWash (the tunnel takes the ticket at the front of the spool and begins the
wash, having re-checked that its terminal is still commissioned and its revision is still
current), DropTicket (the tunnel takes a ticket off the front and discards it because its
terminal has been decommissioned or its revision has been superseded), FinishWash (the
wash completes and the tunnel goes idle), ReviseProgramme (the wash programme revision is
advanced while the tunnel is idle), Commission (a terminal is brought into the till
system), Decommission (a terminal is taken out of the till system, which is not permitted
while its ticket is the running wash), and GoSilent (the one terminal that can fail
silently loses its till link).
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the tunnel is running a wash, that wash belongs to a terminal that is still commissioned and carries the wash programme revision currently in force.

---- MODULE W4Od17m3p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Handlers, NumSlots, MaxEpoch

Slots == 1..NumSlots
NoLeader == "vacant"
NoPermit == <<0, 0>>

VARIABLES leader, epoch, permit, occupied, inService

vars == <<leader, epoch, permit, occupied, inService>>

\* A permit is only worth anything while its epoch is the leadership now in force.
Promised(s) == \E h \in Handlers : permit[h] = <<s, epoch>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ leader \in Handlers \cup {NoLeader}
  /\ epoch \in 1..MaxEpoch
  /\ permit \in [Handlers -> (Slots \X (1..MaxEpoch)) \cup {NoPermit}]
  /\ occupied \subseteq Slots
  /\ inService \subseteq Slots

Init ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ epoch = 1
  /\ permit = [h \in Handlers |-> NoPermit]
  /\ occupied = {}
  /\ inService = Slots

GrantPermit(h, s) ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ permit[h] = NoPermit
  /\ s \in inService
  /\ s \notin occupied
  /\ ~Promised(s)
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![h] = <<s, epoch>>]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, occupied, inService>>

Inject(h) ==
  /\ permit[h] # NoPermit
  /\ permit[h][2] = epoch
  /\ permit[h][1] \in inService
  /\ permit[h][1] \notin occupied
  /\ occupied' = occupied \cup {permit[h][1]}
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![h] = NoPermit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, inService>>

ExpirePermit(h) ==
  /\ permit[h] # NoPermit
  /\ permit[h][2] # epoch
  /\ permit' = [permit EXCEPT ![h] = NoPermit]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, occupied, inService>>

Unload(s) ==
  /\ s \in occupied
  /\ occupied' = occupied \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, permit, inService>>

\* Capacity shrinks only where nothing is riding and nothing has been promised.
TakeOutOfService(s) ==
  /\ s \in inService
  /\ s \notin occupied
  /\ ~Promised(s)
  /\ inService' = inService \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, permit, occupied>>

ReturnToService(s) ==
  /\ s \notin inService
  /\ inService' = inService \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, epoch, permit, occupied>>

Elect(h) ==
  /\ leader = NoLeader
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
  /\ leader' = h
  /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<permit, occupied, inService>>

\* Modelled only while a replacement election is still affordable.
LeaderDrop ==
  /\ leader # NoLeader
  /\ epoch < MaxEpoch - 1
  /\ leader' = NoLeader
  /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, permit, occupied, inService>>

Next ==
  \/ \E h \in Handlers, s \in Slots : GrantPermit(h, s)
  \/ \E h \in Handlers : Inject(h) \/ ExpirePermit(h) \/ Elect(h)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : Unload(s) \/ TakeOutOfService(s) \/ ReturnToService(s)
  \/ LeaderDrop

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A s \in Slots : WF_vars(Unload(s))

LoopRidesOnlyServiceableSlots == occupied \subseteq inService

BagsLeaveTheLoop ==
  \A s \in Slots : (s \in occupied) ~> (s \notin occupied)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Handlers = {h1, h2}
    NumSlots = 2
    MaxEpoch = 4
INVARIANT LoopRidesOnlyServiceableSlots
PROPERTY BagsLeaveTheLoop
nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags onto a sorting loop. The loop is divided into
numbered carrier slots, and a bag can only ride the loop if it is sitting in a slot that is
actually in service. Slots go out of service and come back during the day -- a carrier
plate cracks, a section is isolated for a belt splice, an engineer releases it again -- so
the loop's real capacity moves around underneath the traffic. A slot may only be taken out
of service when nothing is riding in it and nothing has been promised it.

Injection is not decided by the handlers. One routing controller acts as leader and issues
injection permits, and each permit names a slot and carries the epoch of the leadership
that issued it. If the leader drops out, a replacement takes over under a fresh epoch, and
every permit stamped with the old epoch is thereby void: a handler holding one must
discard it rather than inject against it, because the slot it names may since have been
isolated or promised to somebody else. The leader will only issue a permit for a slot that
is in service, unoccupied, and not already promised to another handler, and the handler
re-checks all of that at the moment it injects.

The full action set is: GrantPermit (the acting leader promises a handler a slot that is in
service, empty and unpromised, stamping the permit with the current epoch), Inject (a
handler with a current-epoch permit puts a bag into the named slot, the slot still being in
service and empty), ExpirePermit (a handler discards a permit whose epoch has been
superseded), Unload (a bag rides round to its chute and leaves its slot), TakeOutOfService
(a slot with nothing in it and nothing promised on it is isolated, shrinking the loop's
capacity), ReturnToService (an isolated slot is brought back), Elect (a controller takes
the vacant leader seat under a new epoch), and LeaderDrop (the acting leader falls off the
control network, vacating the seat).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every bag riding the sorting loop is in a carrier slot that is currently in service, so the loop never carries more bags than it has serviceable slots.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bag that gets onto the sorting loop eventually leaves its slot at its chute.

---- MODULE W4Od6m7p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumCars, ZoneLimit, MaxTrips

Cars == 1..NumCars
Dispatchers == 1..2
NoCopy == {0}

\* The lower half of the bank belongs to one dispatcher, the upper half to the other.
Owner(c) == IF 2 * c <= NumCars THEN 1 ELSE 2

VARIABLES zone, copy, waiting, trips

vars == <<zone, copy, waiting, trips>>

TypeOK ==
  /\ zone \subseteq Cars
  /\ copy \in [Dispatchers -> SUBSET (0..NumCars)]
  /\ waiting \subseteq Cars
  /\ trips \in 0..MaxTrips

Init ==
  /\ zone = {}
  /\ copy = [d \in Dispatchers |-> NoCopy]
  /\ waiting = {}
  /\ trips = 0

CallCar(c) ==
  /\ c \notin waiting
  /\ c \notin zone
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {c}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zone, copy, trips>>

CopyRegister(d) ==
  /\ copy[d] = NoCopy
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![d] = zone]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zone, waiting, trips>>

\* The swap goes in only against a register still identical to the copy taken, which
\* is what stops the two dispatchers filling the zone twice over.
Admit(d, c) ==
  /\ copy[d] # NoCopy
  /\ copy[d] = zone
  /\ Owner(c) = d
  /\ c \in waiting
  /\ c \notin copy[d]
  /\ Cardinality(copy[d]) < ZoneLimit
  /\ zone' = zone \cup {c}
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {c}
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![d] = NoCopy]
  /\ UNCHANGED trips

Retry(d) ==
  /\ copy[d] # NoCopy
  /\ \/ copy[d] # zone
     \/ Cardinality(copy[d]) >= ZoneLimit
     \/ ~\E c \in waiting : Owner(c) = d /\ c \notin copy[d]
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![d] = NoCopy]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<zone, waiting, trips>>

LeaveZone(c) ==
  /\ c \in zone
  /\ trips < MaxTrips
  /\ zone' = zone \ {c}
  /\ trips' = trips + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<copy, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E c \in Cars : CallCar(c) \/ LeaveZone(c)
  \/ \E d \in Dispatchers : CopyRegister(d) \/ Retry(d)
  \/ \E d \in Dispatchers, c \in Cars : Admit(d, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

ZoneWithinRescueLimit == Cardinality(zone) <= ZoneLimit

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumCars = 4
    ZoneLimit = 2
    MaxTrips = 2
INVARIANT ZoneWithinRescueLimit
nl:
The elevator bank in a skyscraper has an express shaft zone that only a limited number of
cars may occupy at once -- the zone shares one ventilation and rescue corridor, and beyond
that number the corridor cannot be cleared in time. Which cars are in the zone is held in a
single compare-and-swap register on the group controller: the register holds the whole set
of cars currently inside.

Two dispatch instances share that one register. The low-rise dispatcher owns the lower
cars and the high-rise dispatcher owns the upper ones, and neither knows anything about
what the other is about to do; the register is their only point of contact. A dispatcher
that wants to send one of its cars into the zone first takes a copy of the register, checks
against that copy that the zone has room and that its car is not already inside, and then
swaps the enlarged set in. The swap is accepted only if the register still holds exactly
the set the dispatcher copied. If the other dispatcher got there first the copy is stale,
the swap is rejected, and the dispatcher takes a fresh copy and tries again.

The full action set is: CallCar (a car is called and starts waiting for the express zone),
CopyRegister (a dispatcher takes a copy of the register's current set of cars in the zone),
Admit (a dispatcher whose copy still matches the register, and whose copy showed both room
in the zone and its own waiting car outside it, swaps that car into the register), Retry (a
dispatcher whose copy no longer matches the register, or whose copy showed the zone
already full, throws the copy away), and LeaveZone (a car finishes its express run and is
taken out of the register).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of cars in the express shaft zone never exceeds the number the rescue corridor can clear.

---- MODULE W4Od11m6p0t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumOperators, MaxClock, MaxRevokes

Operators == 1..NumOperators
NoHolder == 0

VARIABLES clock, holder, deadline, rendering, asked, revokes

vars == <<clock, holder, deadline, rendering, asked, revokes>>

\* An expired lease confers nothing, so the set of operators entitled to the RIP is
\* empty as soon as the clock reaches the deadline.
Entitled == IF holder # NoHolder /\ clock < deadline THEN {holder} ELSE {}

TypeOK ==
  /\ clock \in 0..MaxClock
  /\ holder \in Operators \cup {NoHolder}
  /\ deadline \in 0..MaxClock
  /\ rendering \subseteq Operators
  /\ asked \subseteq Operators
  /\ revokes \in 0..MaxRevokes

Init ==
  /\ clock = 0
  /\ holder = NoHolder
  /\ deadline = 0
  /\ rendering = {}
  /\ asked = {}
  /\ revokes = 0

RequestRIP(o) ==
  /\ o \notin asked
  /\ asked' = asked \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, rendering, revokes>>

GrantLease(o, d) ==
  /\ holder = NoHolder
  /\ o \in asked
  /\ holder' = o
  /\ clock' = 0
  /\ deadline' = d
  /\ asked' = asked \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<rendering, revokes>>

StartJob(o) ==
  /\ holder = o
  /\ clock < deadline
  /\ o \notin rendering
  /\ rendering' = rendering \cup {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, asked, revokes>>

StopJob(o) ==
  /\ o \in rendering
  /\ rendering' = rendering \ {o}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, holder, deadline, asked, revokes>>

\* A job must fit inside its lease: the clock cannot run past a live rendering.
Tick ==
  /\ clock < MaxClock
  /\ (rendering = {} \/ clock + 1 < deadline)
  /\ clock' = clock + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, deadline, rendering, asked, revokes>>

ExpireLease ==
  /\ holder # NoHolder
  /\ clock >= deadline
  /\ rendering = {}
  /\ holder' = NoHolder
  /\ deadline' = 0
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, rendering, asked, revokes>>

\* The privileged revocation cuts the lease and the running job in one movement.
ManagerRevoke ==
  /\ revokes < MaxRevokes
  /\ holder # NoHolder
  /\ holder' = NoHolder
  /\ deadline' = 0
  /\ rendering' = {}
  /\ revokes' = revokes + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, asked>>

Next ==
  \/ \E o \in Operators : RequestRIP(o) \/ StartJob(o) \/ StopJob(o)
  \/ \E o \in Operators, d \in 1..MaxClock : GrantLease(o, d)
  \/ Tick \/ ExpireLease \/ ManagerRevoke

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A o \in Operators : WF_vars(StopJob(o))
  /\ SF_vars(Tick)
  /\ SF_vars(ExpireLease)

RIPRunsOnlyUnderALiveLease == rendering \subseteq Entitled

LeasesAreGivenUp ==
  (holder # NoHolder) ~> (holder = NoHolder)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumOperators = 2
    MaxClock = 2
    MaxRevokes = 1
INVARIANT RIPRunsOnlyUnderALiveLease
PROPERTY LeasesAreGivenUp
nl:
A print shop job spooler has one raster image processor, and the RIP is the critical
resource: it can only be rendering for one operator at a time. Access is handed out as a
lease rather than a lock. When the RIP is free an operator that has asked for it is given
a lease with a deadline measured on the shop clock, and the lease is only good until that
deadline passes. An operator may only put work on the RIP while it holds a lease whose
deadline has not yet been reached; the moment the lease expires it grants nothing at all,
which is what stops a forgotten holder blocking the machine forever. Correspondingly the
shop clock is only allowed to advance past a job that is actually rendering if the deadline
is still ahead of it -- a job must be sized to finish inside its lease.

The shop manager has a privilege on top of this: the manager can revoke a lease outright
without waiting for its deadline, pulling any running job off the RIP at the same moment.
That privilege is rationed to a small number of uses, so it cannot be leaned on as a
substitute for the ordinary lease cycle.

The full action set is: RequestRIP (an operator asks for the RIP), GrantLease (the RIP is
free, so a waiting operator is given a lease with a deadline on the shop clock), StartJob
(an operator whose lease has not yet expired puts a job on the RIP), StopJob (an operator
takes its job off the RIP), Tick (the shop clock advances, which is only permitted if
nothing is rendering or the deadline is still ahead), ExpireLease (a lease whose deadline
has been reached, with nothing rendering under it, is given up), and ManagerRevoke (the
shop manager tears up the current lease and pulls any running job off the RIP, using one of
the rationed revocations).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the only operator ever rendering on the RIP is the holder of a lease whose deadline has not yet been reached.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every lease that is handed out is eventually given up again, so the RIP always comes back free.

---- MODULE W4Od11m4p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Jobs, NumSlots, SpoolLimit

Slots == 1..NumSlots
Unowned == "unowned"
Notes == Jobs \X Slots
Spools == UNION {[1..n -> Notes] : n \in 0..SpoolLimit}

VARIABLES ledger, spool, waiting, printing

vars == <<ledger, spool, waiting, printing>>

\* Slots that already have a note riding down to the press floor.
Riding == {spool[i][2] : i \in 1..Len(spool)}

Drop(sq, i) == SubSeq(sq, 1, i - 1) \o SubSeq(sq, i + 1, Len(sq))

TypeOK ==
  /\ ledger \in [Slots -> Jobs \cup {Unowned}]
  /\ spool \in Spools
  /\ waiting \subseteq Jobs
  /\ printing \subseteq Slots

Init ==
  /\ ledger = [s \in Slots |-> Unowned]
  /\ spool = << >>
  /\ waiting = {}
  /\ printing = {}

SubmitJob(j) ==
  /\ j \notin waiting
  /\ ~\E i \in 1..Len(spool) : spool[i][1] = j
  /\ \A s \in Slots : ledger[s] # j
  /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, spool, printing>>

\* A slot is promised once and once only: not if owned, not if already riding.
WriteNote(j, s) ==
  /\ j \in waiting
  /\ Len(spool) < SpoolLimit
  /\ ledger[s] = Unowned
  /\ s \notin Riding
  /\ spool' = Append(spool, <<j, s>>)
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, printing>>

\* Backpressure: with the spool at its limit the shop turns work away.
RefuseJob(j) ==
  /\ j \in waiting
  /\ Len(spool) = SpoolLimit
  /\ waiting' = waiting \ {j}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, spool, printing>>

\* Runners arrive in any order, so any note in the spool may be the next to land.
DeliverNote(i) ==
  /\ i \in 1..Len(spool)
  /\ ledger[spool[i][2]] = Unowned
  /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![spool[i][2]] = spool[i][1]]
  /\ spool' = Drop(spool, i)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, printing>>

TearUpNote(i) ==
  /\ i \in 1..Len(spool)
  /\ ledger[spool[i][2]] # Unowned
  /\ spool' = Drop(spool, i)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, waiting, printing>>

StartPress(s) ==
  /\ ledger[s] # Unowned
  /\ s \notin printing
  /\ printing' = printing \cup {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, spool, waiting>>

ReleaseSlot(s) ==
  /\ s \in printing
  /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![s] = Unowned]
  /\ printing' = printing \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<spool, waiting>>

Next ==
  \/ \E j \in Jobs : SubmitJob(j) \/ RefuseJob(j)
  \/ \E j \in Jobs, s \in Slots : WriteNote(j, s)
  \/ \E i \in 1..SpoolLimit : DeliverNote(i) \/ TearUpNote(i)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : StartPress(s) \/ ReleaseSlot(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OwnedSlotsHaveNoNoteRiding ==
  \A s \in Slots : ledger[s] # Unowned => s \notin Riding

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Jobs = {j1, j2}
    NumSlots = 2
    SpoolLimit = 2
INVARIANT OwnedSlotsHaveNoNoteRiding
nl:
A print shop job spooler allocates press slots -- the numbered windows in the day's press
schedule -- and a slot must never end up allocated to two jobs. The spooler keeps a wall
ledger saying which job, if any, owns each slot. Allocations are not applied on the spot:
the spooler writes a promise into a bounded spool of allocation notes and the notes are
carried down to the press floor by runners. The spool holds only so many notes at once,
and when it is full the spooler refuses to take on further work -- backpressure -- rather
than promising more than it can carry.

The runners do not keep order. A note written first can easily reach the press floor after
a note written later, so the spooler cannot rely on notes landing in the sequence it wrote
them. Its discipline is therefore to promise a slot only once: it will not write a note for
a slot that the ledger already shows as owned, nor for a slot that already has a note
riding down with a runner. A note that reaches the floor for a slot the ledger has since
recorded against somebody else is torn up rather than applied.

The full action set is: SubmitJob (a job is taken on and starts waiting for a slot),
WriteNote (the spooler promises a waiting job a slot that is neither owned in the ledger
nor already promised in the spool, and adds a note to the spool provided the spool is below
its limit), RefuseJob (a waiting job is turned away because the spool is at its limit),
DeliverNote (a runner arrives with some note, in no particular order, and the ledger
records that slot against that job), TearUpNote (a runner arrives with a note for a slot
the ledger already shows as owned, and the note is discarded), StartPress (a job whose
slot is recorded in the ledger puts the press to work on that slot), and ReleaseSlot (the
press finishes with a slot and the ledger gives it back).
SAFETY PROPERTY: no press slot that the ledger already shows as owned still has an allocation note riding down to the press floor, so a slot is never promised to a second job.

---- MODULE W4Od12m1p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS NumSites, MaxLog, MaxKind

Sites == 1..NumSites
Ring(i) == IF i = NumSites THEN 1 ELSE i + 1
Nothing == 0

VARIABLES ledger, copy, token, staged

vars == <<ledger, copy, token, staged>>

Level(s) == Len(copy[s]) = Len(ledger)

TypeOK ==
  /\ ledger \in UNION {[1..n -> 1..MaxKind] : n \in 0..MaxLog}
  /\ copy \in [Sites -> UNION {[1..n -> 1..MaxKind] : n \in 0..MaxLog}]
  /\ token \in Sites
  /\ staged \in [Sites -> 0..MaxKind]

Init ==
  /\ ledger = << >>
  /\ copy = [s \in Sites |-> << >>]
  /\ token = 1
  /\ staged = [s \in Sites |-> Nothing]

StageMovement(s, k) ==
  /\ staged[s] = Nothing
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![s] = k]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, copy, token>>

\* Writing from behind is how a movement gets overwritten, so the writer must be
\* level with the master before it may append.
CommitMovement(s) ==
  /\ token = s
  /\ staged[s] # Nothing
  /\ Level(s)
  /\ Len(ledger) < MaxLog
  /\ ledger' = Append(ledger, staged[s])
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![s] = Append(copy[s], staged[s])]
  /\ staged' = [staged EXCEPT ![s] = Nothing]
  /\ UNCHANGED token

PullEntry(s) ==
  /\ Len(copy[s]) < Len(ledger)
  /\ copy' = [copy EXCEPT ![s] = Append(copy[s], ledger[Len(copy[s]) + 1])]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, token, staged>>

\* The turn is kept while the holder still has something staged.
PassToken ==
  /\ staged[token] = Nothing
  /\ token' = Ring(token)
  /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, copy, staged>>

Archive ==
  /\ Len(ledger) > 0
  /\ \A s \in Sites : Level(s)
  /\ ledger' = << >>
  /\ copy' = [s \in Sites |-> << >>]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<token, staged>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Sites, k \in 1..MaxKind : StageMovement(s, k)
  \/ \E s \in Sites : CommitMovement(s) \/ PullEntry(s)
  \/ PassToken
  \/ Archive

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ SF_vars(PassToken)
  /\ \A s \in Sites : WF_vars(CommitMovement(s))
  /\ \A s \in Sites : WF_vars(PullEntry(s))
  /\ WF_vars(Archive)

CopiesAreLeadingRuns ==
  \A s \in Sites : copy[s] = SubSeq(ledger, 1, Len(copy[s]))

StagedMovementsGetWritten ==
  \A s \in Sites : (staged[s] # Nothing) ~> (staged[s] = Nothing)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumSites = 2
    MaxLog = 2
    MaxKind = 2
INVARIANT CopiesAreLeadingRuns
PROPERTY StagedMovementsGetWritten
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker keeps one master ledger of donor-unit movements, written as
an append-only run of entries, and each collection site keeps its own copy of that ledger
so it can work when the line to head office is quiet. The whole point of the arrangement is
that no movement a site has written is ever lost or overwritten: every site's copy must be
an exact leading run of the master ledger, never a divergent one.

The right to write to the master is passed around the sites as a token, in a fixed ring.
A site that has a movement to record stages it locally and then waits for the token to
come round; it does not hand the token on while it still has something staged, so its turn
is not skipped. When the token arrives, the site may only write into the master if its own
copy has already been brought fully up to date with everything written before it -- writing
from behind is exactly how a movement gets overwritten.

Sites can be slow. None of them ever fails or drops out of the ring, but a site can be
several entries behind, and it pulls entries down one at a time until it is level. Because
the master run has a finite length, there is also an end-of-day archive: once every site's
copy is level with the master, the master run and all the copies are archived together and
the ledger starts empty again.

The full action set is: StageMovement (a site takes down a donor-unit movement and holds it
locally), CommitMovement (the site holding the token, whose copy is fully level with the
master, appends its staged movement to the master ledger and to its own copy at the same
moment), PullEntry (a site that is behind pulls the next entry of the master ledger into
its copy), PassToken (a site with nothing staged hands the token to the next site in the
ring), and Archive (with every copy level with the master, the run is archived and the
ledger starts empty again).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every site's copy of the ledger is exactly a leading run of the master ledger, so no recorded movement is ever lost or overwritten.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every movement a site stages is eventually written into the master ledger.

---- MODULE W4Od18m0p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS NumGuests, TableSize, MaxRevision, MaxRefusals

Guests == 1..NumGuests
Apps == 1..2
NoApp == 0
NoRead == <<MaxRevision + 1, 0>>

VARIABLES revision, reading, issuer, refusals

vars == <<revision, reading, issuer, refusals>>

\* issuer[g] records which of the two apps issued g's credential, 0 if g has none.
Live == {g \in Guests : issuer[g] # NoApp}

TypeOK ==
  /\ revision \in 0..MaxRevision
  /\ reading \in [Apps -> (0..(MaxRevision + 1)) \X (0..NumGuests)]
  /\ issuer \in [Guests -> 0..2]
  /\ refusals \in 0..MaxRefusals

Init ==
  /\ revision = 0
  /\ reading = [a \in Apps |-> NoRead]
  /\ issuer = [g \in Guests |-> NoApp]
  /\ refusals = 0

ReadTable(a) ==
  /\ reading[a] = NoRead
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![a] = <<revision, Cardinality(Live)>>]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, issuer, refusals>>

\* The app issues against the count it noted; the revision match is what makes that
\* stale count trustworthy, even with the other app writing the same table.
IssueCredential(a, g) ==
  /\ reading[a] # NoRead
  /\ reading[a][1] = revision
  /\ reading[a][2] < TableSize
  /\ issuer[g] = NoApp
  /\ revision < MaxRevision
  /\ issuer' = [issuer EXCEPT ![g] = a]
  /\ revision' = revision + 1
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![a] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED refusals

RefuseGuest(a) ==
  /\ reading[a] # NoRead
  /\ reading[a][1] = revision
  /\ reading[a][2] >= TableSize
  /\ refusals < MaxRefusals
  /\ refusals' = refusals + 1
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![a] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, issuer>>

StartOver(a) ==
  /\ reading[a] # NoRead
  /\ \/ reading[a][1] # revision
     \/ reading[a][2] >= TableSize
     \/ revision = MaxRevision
     \/ \A g \in Guests : issuer[g] # NoApp
  /\ reading' = [reading EXCEPT ![a] = NoRead]
  /\ UNCHANGED <<revision, issuer, refusals>>

RevokeCredential(g) ==
  /\ issuer[g] # NoApp
  /\ revision < MaxRevision
  /\ issuer' = [issuer EXCEPT ![g] = NoApp]
  /\ revision' = revision + 1
  /\ UNCHANGED <<reading, refusals>>

Next ==
  \/ \E a \in Apps : ReadTable(a) \/ RefuseGuest(a) \/ StartOver(a)
  \/ \E a \in Apps, g \in Guests : IssueCredential(a, g)
  \/ \E g \in Guests : RevokeCredential(g)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TableWithinCapacity == Cardinality(Live) <= TableSize

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumGuests = 3
    TableSize = 2
    MaxRevision = 3
    MaxRefusals = 2
INVARIANT TableWithinCapacity
nl:
A smart-home door lock network can only hold a limited number of live guest credentials at
once: the locks share one credential table, and beyond that many entries the table cannot
be pushed out to the hardware. Two independent apps share that one table. The residents'
app issues credentials for their own visitors, and the property manager's app issues them
for contractors and cleaners; neither app knows what the other is doing, and the only thing
they have in common is the table itself.

Neither app locks the table. An app reads it optimistically: it notes the table's revision
number together with how many credentials were live at that moment, and then goes off to
work out who to admit. Every change to the table -- a credential issued, a credential
revoked -- moves the revision number on. When the app finally comes to issue, the write is
accepted only if the revision it noted is still current, which is what proves the count it
noted is still true and there really is a free entry. If the revision has moved, the app's
whole reading is worthless and it starts again; if the reading showed the table already
full, the app turns the request away instead.

The full action set is: ReadTable (an app notes the current revision number and the number
of live credentials), IssueCredential (an app whose noted revision is still current, and
whose noted count showed a free entry, adds a credential for a guest who does not yet have
one, moving the revision on), RefuseGuest (an app whose noted count showed the table
already full turns the request away and records a refusal), StartOver (an app whose noted
revision is no longer current, or which finds no candidate guest or the revision counter
used up for the day, throws its reading away), and RevokeCredential (a live credential is
taken back, moving the revision on).
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of live guest credentials in the shared table never exceeds the number of entries the locks can hold.

---- MODULE W4Od0m3p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS NumCoords, NumSlots, NumTeams, MaxLead

Coords == 1..NumCoords
Slots == 1..NumSlots
Teams == 1..NumTeams
Vacant == 0
Empty == 0

VARIABLES lead, leadNo, wall, commitments, paging

vars == <<lead, leadNo, wall, commitments, paging>>

Travelling(s) == \E m \in paging : m[1] = s

TypeOK ==
  /\ lead \in Coords \cup {Vacant}
  /\ leadNo \in 1..MaxLead
  /\ wall \in [Slots -> Teams \cup {Empty}]
  /\ commitments \subseteq Slots
  /\ paging \subseteq (Slots \X Teams \X (1..MaxLead))

Init ==
  /\ lead = Vacant
  /\ leadNo = 1
  /\ wall = [s \in Slots |-> Empty]
  /\ commitments = {}
  /\ paging = {}

Commit(s, t) ==
  /\ lead # Vacant
  /\ s \notin commitments
  /\ wall[s] = Empty
  /\ ~Travelling(s)
  /\ commitments' = commitments \cup {s}
  /\ paging' = paging \cup {<<s, t, leadNo>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, leadNo, wall>>

\* The leadership number on the slip is what makes an out-of-order delivery safe.
Deliver(s, t, n) ==
  /\ <<s, t, n>> \in paging
  /\ n = leadNo
  /\ wall[s] = Empty
  /\ wall' = [wall EXCEPT ![s] = t]
  /\ paging' = paging \ {<<s, t, n>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, leadNo, commitments>>

DiscardSlip(s, t, n) ==
  /\ <<s, t, n>> \in paging
  /\ (n # leadNo \/ wall[s] # Empty)
  /\ paging' = paging \ {<<s, t, n>>}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, leadNo, wall, commitments>>

FreeSlot(s) ==
  /\ wall[s] # Empty
  /\ wall' = [wall EXCEPT ![s] = Empty]
  /\ commitments' = commitments \ {s}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, leadNo, paging>>

\* A new lead can only see the board, so its list leaves out anything in transit.
TakeLead(c) ==
  /\ lead = Vacant
  /\ leadNo < MaxLead
  /\ lead' = c
  /\ leadNo' = leadNo + 1
  /\ commitments' = {s \in Slots : wall[s] # Empty}
  /\ UNCHANGED <<wall, paging>>

LeadDropsOut ==
  /\ lead # Vacant
  /\ leadNo < MaxLead - 1
  /\ lead' = Vacant
  /\ UNCHANGED <<leadNo, wall, commitments, paging>>

Next ==
  \/ \E s \in Slots, t \in Teams : Commit(s, t)
  \/ \E s \in Slots, t \in Teams, n \in 1..MaxLead : Deliver(s, t, n) \/ DiscardSlip(s, t, n)
  \/ \E s \in Slots : FreeSlot(s)
  \/ \E c \in Coords : TakeLead(c)
  \/ LeadDropsOut

Spec ==
  /\ Init
  /\ [][Next]_vars
  /\ \A s \in Slots, t \in Teams, n \in 1..MaxLead :
       WF_vars(Deliver(s, t, n) \/ DiscardSlip(s, t, n))

BoardIsTracked ==
  {s \in Slots : wall[s] # Empty} \subseteq commitments

SlipsAreResolved ==
  \A s \in Slots : Travelling(s) ~> ~Travelling(s)

====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    NumCoords = 2
    NumSlots = 2
    NumTeams = 2
    MaxLead = 4
INVARIANT BoardIsTracked
PROPERTY SlipsAreResolved
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler hands out theatre slots, and a slot must never be
given to two surgical teams. Slots are booked on the theatre wall board, which is the
physical record of who has what. The board is not written directly by the schedulers: one
coordinator acts as lead, and the lead keeps its own commitment list of the slots it has
already given away, only ever committing a slot that is not on that list, not already on
the wall board, and does not already have a booking slip travelling towards the board.

Booking slips go to the theatre floor through the hospital's paging system, which does not
preserve order -- a slip written first can reach the board minutes after one written later.
Each slip carries the number of the leadership under which it was written. If the lead
coordinator drops out, another takes over under a new leadership number and rebuilds its
commitment list from what is actually on the wall board, which necessarily leaves out
anything still travelling. That is why a slip is only honoured when its leadership number
is the one currently in force: a slip from a superseded lead names a slot the new lead has
never committed to, and honouring it would put a booking on the board that nobody is
tracking, ready to be given away a second time.

The full action set is: Commit (the acting lead gives a waiting team a slot that is not on
its commitment list, not on the wall board and not already travelling, and sends a booking
slip through the paging system), Deliver (a slip reaches the board while its leadership
number is the one in force and the slot is still empty, so the booking goes up),
DiscardSlip (a slip reaches the board carrying a superseded leadership number or naming a
slot already taken, and is thrown away), FreeSlot (a case finishes and the slot comes off
both the wall board and the lead's commitment list), TakeLead (a coordinator takes the
vacant lead role under a new leadership number and rebuilds its commitment list from the
wall board), and LeadDropsOut (the acting lead is called away and the lead role falls
vacant).
SAFETY PROPERTY: every booking on the theatre wall board is a slot the acting lead has on its commitment list, so no slot is ever given away a second time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: every booking slip put into the paging system is eventually resolved, either going up on the wall board or being thrown away.
